operations.name: extrude_circle
operations.summary: A solid cylinder centered on the origin.
operations.details:
Creates a solid cylinder: a circle on a plane, extruded. It is the operation for pins, dowels, bushes, discs.

On a part that already has a body, the new cylinder merges with the bodies it touches (merge and automatic body selection are on, as the guide describes them); it cannot merge with a body it does not touch, and the document state counts the bodies afterwards.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

height_mm.description: length of the cylinder, in mm

operations.name: extrude_profile
operations.summary: Any shape, given by contours, extruded: the general way to make the first body.
operations.details:
Extrudes ANY SHAPE, given as a list of vertices. It is the operation for everything that is not a rectangle or a circle: shaped brackets, angle brackets, gussets, angles, and HOLLOW profiles — tubes, pipes, C sections — which are made with TWO contours, an outer one and an inner one.

The first contour is the outer edge; the ones after it are voids inside it. Each contour closes by itself: the last vertex joins the first, do not repeat it.

If the shape you need has a name (a gear, a tubular section), see whether a dedicated operation exists: it is easier for whoever confirms to check, because it shows the dimensions instead of a list of points.

The result says whether the sketch is locked: true only when every segment of the sketch got its FIXED relation, counted again after the rebuild. It also carries «fixed_relations» (how many were added) and, when the sketch is not locked, «sketch_lock_note» with the reason.

WITH «dimensions»: «driven» the sketch is not locked: every vertex gets a horizontal and a vertical dimension from the origin, and a circle the two of its centre and the one of its size, so that a variable can move them («link_dimension» with the names). «vertex_dimensions» lists, for each vertex, «x» and «y»: the name of the dimension (for example «D3@Sketch1»), or «on_axis» when the vertex sits on the axis and a relation keeps it there: that coordinate cannot be driven, no variable moves it off the axis, and «warning_dimensions» says so. A dimension is a distance: a vertex at x = -30 has a dimension of 30 and «x_side» «negative»; driving it keeps the vertex on its side, and no value carries it across the axis. «sketch_fully_defined» says whether SOLIDWORKS reads the sketch as fully defined. Straight contours and circles only, at most 100 vertices.

On a part that already has a body, the new shape merges with the bodies it touches (merge and automatic body selection are on, as the guide describes them); it cannot merge with a body it does not touch, and the document state counts the bodies afterwards.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right. WHERE THE CONTOUR'S AXES GO (brief R7): «sketch_axes» in the answer names, for the plane used, the model axis each contour axis runs along and the direction of the extrusion.

contours.description:
The FIRST contour is the outer edge, the following ones are the voids inside it.

Each contour can have TWO forms:
1) a closed polyline: a list of vertices, for example [[0,0],[100,0],[100,60],[0,60]]. The last vertex joins the first by itself: do NOT repeat it.
2) a CIRCLE, and for a hole or a round bar you must use this and not a polyline with many sides: {"circle": [x_center, y_center], "diameter_mm": 20}. The two numbers in brackets are the center. A circle approximated by segments has material inside the circumference, and a shaft does not fit in it.

Example, PIPE outer diameter 60 wall 5:
[{"circle": [0, 0], "diameter_mm": 60}, {"circle": [0, 0], "diameter_mm": 50}]
Example, SQUARE TUBE 80x80 wall 5:
[[[-40,-40],[40,-40],[40,40],[-40,40]], [[-35,-35],[35,-35],[35,35],[-35,35]]]

items.description: a polyline (list of [x_mm, y_mm]) or a circle ({"circle": [x, y], "diameter_mm": d})

thickness_mm.description: how far it is extruded, in mm

symmetric.description: extrusion half on one side and half on the other of the plane (default: no)

dimensions.description: «fixed» (default): the sketch locked where it is with FIXED relations. «driven» (brief R5): a dimension from the origin to every vertex, named in «vertex_dimensions», so that «link_dimension» can tie a width or a position to a variable. Straight contours and circles only, at most 100 vertices.

operations.precondition: an open part (empty, or with bodies to add to)

operations.name: extrude_regions
operations.summary: Several regions of one plane extruded to different heights in one step: a height map.
operations.details:
Extrudes SEVERAL REGIONS of one plane, each to its own height, in one step: a stepped plate, the floor of a channel at three depths, a height map. It does what several «extrude_profile» on the same plane would do, with one reading and one confirmation for all of them.

Each region has its «contours» (the same form as «extrude_profile»: the first is the outer edge, the ones after it are voids inside it) and its «height_mm». Every region is checked before the first is drawn; then each one becomes a sketch and an extrusion, merged with the bodies it touches. Regions that overlap merge: the volume counts the overlap once, at the greater height.

The answer lists, for each region, the feature, the height and «depth_dimension»: the name of the dimension of its height, read from the feature (for example «D1@Boss-Extrude2», in the language of the installation), ready for «link_dimension» or «parameters». If a region fails after others were drawn, the step stops and says which ones are in the part: one «undo» withdraws the whole step.

plane.description: construction plane of every region: front, top or right; «sketch_axes» in the answer names the model axis each contour axis runs along and the direction of the extrusion.

regions.description: the regions, in the order they are drawn. Each one: «contours» as in «extrude_profile» (polylines of [x_mm, y_mm] or circles), and «height_mm», how far that region is extruded.

contours.description: the first contour is the outer edge, the following ones the voids inside it: a polyline (list of [x_mm, y_mm], the last vertex joins the first by itself) or a circle ({"circle": [x, y], "diameter_mm": d})

height_mm.description: how far this region is extruded, in mm, above zero

operations.name: extrude_rectangle
operations.summary: A solid rectangular plate, the first body of the part.
operations.details:
Creates a rectangular plate: draws a rectangle on a plane and extrudes it. It is the operation for plates, brackets, bases, square flanges.

«plane» takes «front», «top» or «right» (the case of the letters does not matter); any other name is refused, it never falls back to the front plane.

On a part that already has a body, the new plate merges with the bodies it touches (merge and automatic body selection are on, as the guide describes them); it cannot merge with a body it does not touch, and the document state counts the bodies afterwards.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

thickness_mm.description: HOW FAR IT IS EXTRUDED, in mm. For a plate it is the thickness; for a bar or a profile it is the LENGTH. The rectangle is the section, this is how far it goes in depth: an 80x80 bar 1000 long is made with length_mm 80, width_mm 80, thickness_mm 1000.

centered.description: rectangle centered on the origin (default: yes)

operations.name: extrude_section
operations.summary: A bar from a standard section (tubular, round, angle, U, T, flat, hexagon, slot) that is NOT metalwork.
operations.details:
Extrudes a standard section — tubular, round, tube, L angle, U or T section, flat, hexagon, slot — and gets a SOLID BODY with that shape.

IT IS NOT THE METALWORK OPERATION. For a frame element use «structural_member»: an extruded body has the same shape as a bar, but it is not a structural member, so it does NOT generate the cut list, does not carry the name of the profile, and cannot be mitered at 45 degrees at the joints. Whoever goes to the workshop with a part like this does not have the list of bars to cut.

This operation is for when the section is NOT a frame element: a spacer cut from bar stock, a small shaped plate, a part turned from round bar, or a profile that is not in the company library.

The dimensions to give change with the type:
• tubular  width, height, wall
• tube      diameter, wall
• round     diameter
• angle / u / t   width, height, thickness
• flat / slot     width, height
• hexagon   across flats (the width across the flats, not the circumscribed diameter)

«length_mm» is how long the bar is: for an 80x80x5 tubular 1000 long that is width 80, height 80, wall 5, length 1000.

THE EDGES ARE SHARP, and it shows in the weight. A commercial profile has rounded corners, so this section weighs more: an 80x80x5 tubular 1000 long comes out at 1,500,000 mm3 against about 1,443,000 for the real profile, that is 4% more. For the shape nothing changes; if the number you need is the WEIGHT, take the profile from the library with «structural_member».

THE SLOT IS A POLYGON: its two ends are 24 sides each, with the vertices on the circumscribed circle, so that the slot is never narrower than the nominal one. It comes out 0.2% wider (20.043 for 20) and with 0.2% more area. Round and tube are true circles.

The result says whether the sketch is locked: true only when every segment of the sketch got its FIXED relation, counted again after the rebuild. It also carries «fixed_relations» (how many were added) and, when the sketch is not locked, «sketch_lock_note» with the reason.

On a part that already has a body, the new bar merges with the bodies it touches (merge and automatic body selection are on, as the guide describes them); it cannot merge with a body it does not touch, and the document state counts the bodies afterwards.

length_mm.description: how long the bar is, in mm

wall_mm.description: wall thickness, for tubular and tube

thickness_mm.description: thickness of the profile, for angle, U and T

across_flats_mm.description: width across flats of the hexagon

symmetric.description: half on each side of the plane (default: no)

operations.name: revolve
operations.summary: A solid of revolution: bushes, spacers, stepped shafts, flanges, pulleys, handwheels.
operations.details:
Revolves a profile about an axis and gets a body of revolution. It is the operation for everything made on the lathe when the shape VARIES along the axis: stepped shafts, bushes with grooves, flanges, pulleys. For a constant cylinder «extrude_circle» or «extrude_section» are enough, and simpler.

The profile is given with the same CONTOURS as «extrude_profile»: the first is the edge, the following ones are voids.

THE DIFFERENCE IS THE AXIS. The profile is a HALF SECTION, seen from the side as on the lathe: it lies all on one side of the axis, touching it at most. It must NOT cross it — a profile that crosses the axis produces a solid that intersects itself.

Example, stepped shaft: diameter 30 for 40 mm, then diameter 20 for another 30, axis along y=0:
  contours: [[[0,0],[0,15],[40,15],[40,10],[70,10],[70,0]]]
  axis: [[0,0],[70,0]]
The side from (70,0) to (0,0), which closes the polyline, lies ON the axis: this is the normal case, not an error.

Solid body only: for a thin wall draw the inner void as a second contour.

I REFUSE IF THE AXIS IS NOT ON THE PLANE OF THE PROFILE, and if the profile CROSSES the axis. A profile straddling the axis generates a solid that interpenetrates itself: SOLIDWORKS sometimes makes it all the same, and the part that comes out is not the one you wanted.

The result says whether the sketch is locked: true only when every segment of the sketch got its FIXED relation, counted again after the rebuild. It also carries «fixed_relations» (how many were added) and, when the sketch is not locked, «sketch_lock_note» with the reason.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

contours.description: the profile to revolve, same syntax as «extrude_profile»: the first contour is the edge, the following ones are voids. Each contour is a closed polyline of vertices [x_mm, y_mm] (the last one closes by itself, do not repeat it) or {"circle": [x, y], "diameter_mm": d}. It lies all on one side of the axis.

items.description: a polyline (list of [x_mm, y_mm]) or a circle ({"circle": [x, y], "diameter_mm": d})

axis.description: the line of revolution: TWO points [x_mm, y_mm] in the same system as the contours. For a turned part it is almost always the horizontal axis of the drawing, for example [[0,0],[70,0]]. It is not a detail: it decides the final bounding box as much as the vertices of the profile do.

operations.name: spur_gear
operations.summary: An involute gear, with bore and keyway.
operations.details:
Creates a cylindrical SPUR GEAR, from the number of teeth and the module. The tooth profile is an involute and I calculate it: you give only the design data.

With bore_mm you also get the central bore.

I REFUSE IF there are fewer than 17 teeth (with the standard pressure angle of 20 degrees), because a profile correction against root undercut would be needed and I cannot do it. It is a limit of mine, not of mechanics: with a larger pressure angle the minimum goes down (25 degrees: 11 teeth).

The result says whether the sketch is locked: true only when every segment of the sketch got its FIXED relation, counted again after the rebuild. It also carries «fixed_relations» (how many were added) and, when the sketch is not locked, «sketch_lock_note» with the reason.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

module_mm.description: the module m in mm. Pitch diameter = m x z, outside diameter = m x (z+2).

bore_mm.description: diameter of the central bore; leave it out for a solid gear

keyway.description: keyway in the bore, with standard width and depth (ISO/R 773, DIN 6885-1) taken from the diameter of the bore. Do not ask for the dimensions of the keyway: the standard chooses them.

operations.name: slot
operations.summary: An elongated hole: the fastening that can be adjusted at assembly.
operations.details:
Cuts a SLOT in a face: an elongated hole with round ends. It is what lets you ADJUST on site — a bracket with two slots can be lined up, one with two round holes either fits or has to be made again.

THE LENGTH IS OVERALL, END TO END, as it is measured on the part and as it is written on the drawing; the WIDTH is the diameter of the ends, that is, the diameter of the screw plus the clearance. For an M10 that must slide 40 mm: width 11, length 51.

«angle_deg» rotates the slot in the plane of the face: 0 is horizontal, 90 vertical. It is needed when the adjustment must go in a specific direction.

It is not a rectangular pocket. «rectangular_cut» looks like it but has sharp corners, and the screw rattles inside it instead of sliding.

I REFUSE IF ONE OF FOUR CASES APPLIES, and I list them up front because finding out by trying costs a round: the slot is not through and you do not give me the depth; it falls entirely outside the material (I tell you between which coordinates the face lies); it is larger than the face and would cover it all; or length and width are equal -- that is a circle, and here the length is measured end to end.

face_uid.description: a face that already exists, taken from the state

face_ref.description:
the face created by an earlier step of this same plan. Give this OR face_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- pocket_floor: the floor of the pocket (it exists only if the pocket is blind)
- bottom_face: the face on the sketch plane, the bottom of the extrusion
- top_face: the face at the top of the extrusion, the one opposite the sketch plane

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

x_mm.description: MODEL COORDINATES in mm, not face coordinates. Take the two axes that remain after removing the one along the face's normal, in the order X, Y, Z: normal along Z -> x_mm is the model's X and y_mm the Y; normal along Y -> x_mm is the X and y_mm the Z; normal along X -> x_mm is the Y and y_mm the Z. They are the same numbers as the «point_mm» you read in the document state, so you can start from those. The third coordinate is not needed: it is the plane of the face.

anchor.description:
WHAT KEEPS THE SLOT WHERE IT IS WHEN THE PART CHANGES. Without it, x_mm/y_mm are absolute coordinates: if the plate gets longer, the slot stays where it was. For EACH axis, «x» and «y», both required, one of two things: {"edge_uid": "E7", "distance_mm": 20}, the distance from the CENTER to a straight edge of the same face that runs along the other axis; or {"centered_between": ["E3", "E5"]}, halfway between two opposite edges. x_mm/y_mm stay required and must name the same point.

I REFUSE IF an axis is missing; if x_mm/y_mm and the anchor do not say the same point; if the edge is not straight, is not on the face, does not run along the other axis or lies on the edge of a chamfer or of a fillet (the other face of the edge must be planar and perpendicular, and if I cannot look at it I refuse); if the face you work on is not planar; if the distance is less than half the width (the profile would straddle the edge); if, on a centred axis, the profile is wider than the gap between the two edges; if the sketch does not come out fully defined, or does not hold up under a trial change — and then I remove the cut. I also refuse when I cannot do those checks: relations of the sketch I cannot read, or an anchor dimension I cannot read or move (the test would pass without testing anything).

edge_uid.description: a straight edge of the face, from the state, that runs along y_mm

distance_mm.description: from the CENTER of the profile to the edge, measured along x_mm

centered_between.description: two opposite edges of the face, from the state, that run along y_mm: the center stays halfway between them

length_mm.description: TOTAL length, end to end, not the travel. It must be greater than the width.

width_mm.description: width of the slot, that is, the diameter of the round ends

angle_deg.description: rotation in the plane of the face, default 0. If the four tangencies and the equal radii of the slot cannot be counted, or not all of them were born, the response says so in «slot_relations».

operations.name: extrude_on_face
operations.summary: GROWS material from a face: a boss, a lip, a spacer, a tab.
operations.details:
Draws an outline on a face that already exists and extrudes it OUTWARD, adding material to the part.

IT IS THE OPERATION THAT GROWS A BOSS. The others on an existing part remove (holes, cuts, slots), hollow out (shell) or move; «engrave_text» in relief also adds material, but only lettering, and so does «combine_bodies», which joins bodies that already exist. Without this one you cannot make: the sealing lip of a cover, the spacers something rests on, a fixing tab, a post for a screw, a boss around a hole.

THE OUTLINES ARE IN THE COORDINATES OF THE FACE, as for «rectangular_cut»: (0, 0) is the centre of the face. Several nested outlines make a frame — the outer one and the inner one — and that is how you make a lip around an edge instead of a solid block.

«merge» true (the default) fuses the boss with the part. With false a SEPARATE BODY is born: almost never what you want, and the tree grows the same, so you notice only by counting the bodies.

I REFUSE IF the boss adds no material (it grew INTO the part), if, with «merge», the bodies are not the same as before, or if you ask for the «anchor» on more than one outline or on an outline that is neither round nor an axis-aligned rectangle: the point the anchor holds is the centre, and I cannot guess the centre of an arbitrary polygon.

operations.name: hole_wizard
operations.summary: A hole the way a hole is made: guided creation (Hole Wizard), ISO standard, threaded or clearance, counterbored or countersunk, even several holes at once.
operations.details:
THE RIGHT WAY TO MAKE A HOLE: the SolidWorks Hole Wizard, ISO standard. To be preferred ALWAYS over «cylindrical_cut» when the hole houses a screw, a pin or a thread.

It takes the sizes from the standard: you give the size of the screw («M8») and the type, not the diameters. A threaded M8 hole comes out with the 6.8 tap drill and the thread; a clearance M8 comes out 9.

Several identical holes are made in ONE SINGLE call by giving several «positions»: that is how a series of holes is drawn, and in the shop it reads as a single operation.

Each position can carry an «anchor» (a distance from an edge, or the centre between two edges, per axis): then the hole follows the edge when the part changes. I REFUSE IF only some positions carry an anchor (all or none: the holes are in one sketch), if a distance is less than the radius of the hole, or if, on a centred axis, the gap between the two edges is narrower than the hole. The radius is the widest cut: the counterbore for «counterbore», the countersink for «countersink». I know it only once the hole is made, and then I remove the hole. If SOLIDWORKS does not declare the diameter, the response says so in «anchor_fit_not_checked».

I REFUSE IF the hole rebuilds in error or removes no material (for example a position that lies outside the face), and I remove the hole.

y.description: the anchor along y_mm: edge_uid + distance_mm, or centered_between

edge_uid.description: a straight edge of the face, from the state, that runs along x_mm

distance_mm.description: from the CENTER of the profile to the edge, measured along y_mm

centered_between.description: two opposite edges of the face, from the state, that run along x_mm: the center stays halfway between them

through_all.description: default: yes, unless «depth_mm» is given: then the cut stops at that depth

depth_mm.description: the depth of a blind hole, in mm; given alone it makes the hole blind, and with «through_all» true it is not used

operations.name: shell
operations.summary: Hollows out a solid body leaving a wall of constant thickness: boxes, housings, covers.
operations.details:
The shell: takes a solid body and hollows it out, leaving a wall of constant thickness. The faces named in «faces_uid» are REMOVED, that is, they stay open — a single face opens a box on one side, two opposite faces make a tube open at both ends.

The thickness is taken off toward the INSIDE: the outer envelope does not change, as when opening a box. With «outward» the thickness is added on the outside, and it is for when the INNER envelope is the fixed dimension — a compartment that must stay the given size.

A shell with no face removed is a closed hollow body: legitimate but rare, and almost always the sign that a face is missing from the request. That is why it must be confirmed with «fully_closed».

faces_uid.description: the faces to REMOVE (they stay open), taken from the document state

faces_ref.description:
the faces to REMOVE, when they are created by an EARLIER step of this same plan and so have no identifier yet. Give this OR «faces_uid», not both.

One element for each face to open: «make a block and then hollow it from the top» is a single plan.

Allowed kinds:
- top_face: the face at the top of the extrusion, the one opposite the sketch plane
- bottom_face: the face on the sketch plane
- pocket_floor: the floor of a blind pocket
- hole_face: the cylindrical wall of a hole

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

thickness_mm.description: thickness of the wall that remains

outward.description: default no: the thickness is taken off toward the inside and the outer envelope does not change

fully_closed.description: explicit confirmation for a shell with no face removed. Usually a face is missing: use it only if this is really what you need.

operations.name: edit_extrusion
operations.summary: Changes an extrusion or a cut already made: blind -> through all, or another depth.
operations.details:
Changes the definition of an extrusion or an extruded cut that already exists: a blind hole that must become through («through_all»: true), or a different depth («depth_mm»). The part is not redone: the feature changes in its place in the tree, and the ones downstream follow it.

Afterwards I read the definition back (condition and depth), the volume before and after, and the features in error: if the change breaks one downstream, I put it back as it was and I refuse. If the volume does not change I tell you (a blind cut deeper than the material is already through).

I REFUSE IF the feature is not an extrusion or an extruded cut (for any other dimension there is «set_dimension»), if you ask for «through_all» on an extrusion — also on a boss made on a face with «extrude_on_face», which in the state has type «ICE» like the cuts but is an extrusion —, if the extrusion goes in TWO independent directions (I change and read back only the first, and the second would stay as it was), or if you do not give me exactly one of «through_all» and «depth_mm».

feature_uid.description: the feature to change, with the name from the state («feature»). The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

through_all.description: true: the cut goes through everything. Or «depth_mm».

depth_mm.description: the new depth, in mm (blind). Or «through_all».

operations.precondition: a part with an extrusion or an extruded cut

operations.name: reorder_feature
operations.summary: Moves a feature before or after another in the tree, and says how the part changed.
operations.details:
Moves a feature in the tree, before or after another: a shell placed before a hole gives a different part than one placed after (measured: 56485.7 against 51952.38 mm3 on the same box). I give you the order before and after, the volume and the bodies before and after; if the part does not change I tell you.

IF THE MOVE BREAKS A FEATURE DOWNSTREAM I put it back where it was and I refuse.

I REFUSE IF one of the two features is not there or is no longer the one in the state (a name can change, the ID cannot), if «placement» is not «before» or «after», or if SOLIDWORKS does not move it: that happens when it depends on a feature that would come after (a hole before the extrusion it sits on).

feature_uid.description: the feature to move, with the name from the state («feature»). The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

relative_to_uid.description: the feature to put it next to.

operations.precondition: a part with at least two features

operations.name: global_variable
operations.summary: Gives a NAME to a number (wall = 3 mm): the linked dimensions change with it.
operations.details:
Creates or changes a global variable of the part: «wall» = 12 mm, or an expression («2 * "wall" + 1mm»). The dimensions linked with «link_dimension» change when you change it: it is the way to make a part that can be modified without breaking, without repeating the same number in ten places.

After writing it I read it back, and I tell you which dimensions it drives and the volume before and after.

I REFUSE IF the name is not made of letters, digits and «_», if you give me both (or neither) of «value_mm» and «expression», or if SOLIDWORKS does not accept the name: it reserves some in its own language, such as the word for the thickness (the refusal says which) — use for example «wall».

name.description: the name of the variable: letters, digits and «_», starting with a letter.

expression.description: a SOLIDWORKS expression, with the names between double quotes: «2 * "wall" + 1mm». Or «value_mm».

operations.name: link_dimension
operations.summary: Links a dimension to a variable or to a calculation: the equation drives it.
operations.details:
Links a dimension of the part (its name from the state, «D1@Sketch1») to an expression: a global variable («"wall"») or a calculation («2 * "wall" + 1mm»). From then on the equation drives the dimension, and it changes when the variable changes; «set_dimension» no longer changes it.

After the link I read the dimension back: it must equal what the equation says, and I give you the volume before and after.

I REFUSE IF the dimension is not there (I tell you which ones there are) or if SOLIDWORKS does not accept the expression (a variable that does not exist: create it first with «global_variable»).

dimension.description: the name of the dimension, copied from the document state. The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

expression.description: what to link it to, with the names between double quotes: «"wall"», «2 * "wall" + 1mm».

operations.precondition: an open part with at least one dimension

operations.name: parameters
operations.summary: Global variables and dimension links together, in one step: one evaluation, one rebuild.
operations.details:
Writes several global variables and several dimension links in one step: what «global_variable» and «link_dimension» do one at a time, with one evaluation and one rebuild for all of them. The variables are written first, so a link can use a variable of the same step.

Everything is checked before anything is written (the names of the variables, the dimensions that must exist); after the rebuild every value is read back: a variable given in mm must read the same, a linked dimension must equal its equation. I give you each variable, each link with the value before and after, and the volume before and after.

I REFUSE IF a name is not made of letters, digits and «_», if a dimension is not there (I tell you which ones there are) or if SOLIDWORKS does not accept an equation (a reserved name, a variable that does not exist). If one value does not read back, or the part breaks, I put EVERY equation of the step back as it was and tell you whether the part is back.

variables.description: name: value. A number is a length in millimetres («wall»: 12); a text is a SOLIDWORKS expression with the names between double quotes («double»: «2 * "wall" + 1mm»). Names: letters, digits and «_», starting with a letter.

links.description: dimension: expression. The name of the dimension copied from the document state («D1@Boss-Extrude1», in the language of the installation); the expression with the names between double quotes («"wall"», «2 * "wall" + 1mm»).

operations.precondition: an open part (with the dimensions that «links» names)

operations.name: set_dimension
operations.summary: Changes a dimension of a feature that already exists, without redoing anything.
operations.details:
Changes the VALUE of a dimension — a thickness, a depth, a diameter, a radius — on a feature the part already has.

IT IS THE MOST FREQUENT REQUEST IN THE SHOP: «take that hole to M10», «make the thickness 3». Before, the only way was to delete and redo, that is, to lose everything that came after — holes, fillets, ribs built on that geometry.

YOU FIND THE NAME OF THE DIMENSION IN THE DOCUMENT STATE: every feature carries its own, with name and value in mm (for example «D1@Shell1@Part3.Part» = 6). Copy the name as it is.

The value changes in ALL the configurations: changing just one would leave the part different depending on how you look at it.

If the dimension changes but the volume of the part does not, it is said: almost always it means that this dimension does not drive the geometry you had in mind.

I REFUSE IF the new dimension makes an opening break out of the material — a hole or a slot that was inside the part and would open its edge, or two openings that would merge into one: I put the previous value back, and say so. It happens more often than it seems, because a plate drawn centred grows and shrinks FROM ONE SIDE ONLY: shortening it by 50 moves one side by 50, not two sides by 25.

I REFUSE IF with the new dimension a chamfer or a fillet no longer fits — for example a thickness below the side of the chamfer: SOLIDWORKS gives no error, it changes the shape by itself, and the base feature loses a whole face. I put the previous value back and say which chamfer or fillet.

AN ANGULAR DIMENSION (the state writes it in «deg») is changed in DEGREES: «value_mm» carries the degrees, and the answer says «before_deg» and «after_deg» instead of «before_mm» and «now_mm». A dimension the document state lists with its value null (not 0) could not be read from SOLIDWORKS; set_dimension refuses it before changing anything.

I REFUSE IF the dimension is read-only (I do not override those, even if SOLIDWORKS would allow it), driven (they measure, they do not command), or an integer one, like the number of copies of a pattern.

dimension.description: the name of the dimension, copied from the document state. The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

value_mm.description: the new value, in millimetres; in degrees if the dimension is angular

operations.name: dimension_tolerance
operations.summary: The tolerance on a model dimension (±, bilateral, ISO fit), verified and with the right decimals.
operations.details:
Puts the TOLERANCE on a model dimension: symmetric (±value), bilateral (upper and lower deviations) or an ISO fit (class, e.g. H7 for a hole, g6 for a shaft). From the model dimension it reaches the drawing by itself with «model_dimensions».

THE FIT IS VERIFIED: the deviations are computed by SOLIDWORKS, and I check that the width of the tolerance band is the IT grade of the ISO 286-1 table for that diameter (IT5..IT11, up to 500 mm) and that the sign is the one of the letter (H from zero upward, h from zero downward). If it does not match I put it back as it was and tell you.

THE DECIMALS: I set those of the tolerance on the dimension. Measured: without that, an H7 on 10 came out on the drawing as «10 H7 +0 / 0» — in the shop that means «exact». The tolerance decimals are set and read back on EVERY displayed copy of the dimension; one that does not take them is a refusal, and the tolerance is put back and read back. precision_status reports a SetPrecision3 answer of 1, 2 or 4 (about values I leave unchanged).

The answer carries deviations and limits (10.000 / 10.015 for a Ø10 H7).

I REFUSE IF the IT grade is outside 5..11 or the dimension is over 500 mm (I cannot verify them), if a bilateral has the lower above the upper, and when the verification does not match.

dimension.description: the name of the dimension, copied from the document state (e.g. «D1@Sketch2»). The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

fit_class.description: for «fit»: the ISO class, uppercase for a hole (H7), lowercase for a shaft (g6).

operations.name: suppress_feature
operations.summary: SUPPRESSES (turns off) a feature of the tree, without deleting it. It can be turned back on.
operations.details:
Suppresses a feature: the part goes back to how it was without it, but the feature stays in the tree and can be turned back on with «reactivate».

It is the way to go when you want to SEE the part without a feature, without committing to it. To remove it for real there is «delete_feature», which cannot be undone.

THE NAME OF THE FEATURE IS IN THE DOCUMENT STATE, inside «feature» (for example «Cut-Extrude2»). Copy it as it is.

THE CHILDREN ARE SUPPRESSED WITH IT, and that is almost always what you want: suppressing a hole also suppresses its fillets. The answer says which ones were.

AFTERWARDS THE IDENTIFIERS ARE NO LONGER VALID. Suppressing makes faces disappear, and the identifiers (F1, E4) are renumbered by area at every reading: read the part again before the next step.

I REFUSE IF THE FEATURE IS ALREADY SUPPRESSED, and I tell you to use the operation that reactivates it. Suppressing twice does nothing and gives no error: it is the easiest way to believe you changed the part without having touched it.

feature_uid.description: the name of the feature, copied from the document state. The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

reactivate.description: true TURNS BACK ON a suppressed feature, instead of suppressing it. Default: false.

operations.name: delete_feature
operations.summary: DELETES a feature from the tree. It cannot be undone with another operation.
operations.details:
Removes a feature from the tree for good. The sketch it had absorbed goes away with it, so nothing orphaned is left in the tree.

IT CANNOT BE UNDONE with another operation: the only way back is the «undo» tool, and only if you have done nothing else afterwards. The bridge asks the person for a confirmation first when the client can ask (MCP «elicitation»); when it cannot, the plan runs and the answer says in «confirmation» that nobody was asked. If you only want to see the part without that feature, use «suppress_feature», which can be turned back on.

I REFUSE IF ANYTHING DEPENDS ON IT, and I tell you what. Deleting a feature that others depend on would make them all disappear, and SOLIDWORKS does it without asking: if it is really that one you want to remove, first remove what sits on top of it.

THE NAME OF THE FEATURE IS IN THE DOCUMENT STATE, inside «feature». Copy it as it is.

AFTERWARDS THE IDENTIFIERS ARE NO LONGER VALID: read the part again before the next step.

feature_uid.description: the name of the feature, copied from the document state. The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

operations.name: fillet_edges
operations.summary: Constant-radius fillet on one or more edges.
operations.details:
Rounds one or more edges with the same radius. The edges are indicated with the identifiers taken from the document state.

If the edges were renumbered between the reading of the state and now (a hole made in between renumbers them), I find them again by signature: same length at the same place, and I say so in the answer. I REFUSE IF the edge you had seen is no longer as it was — shortened, split — instead of taking the nearest, or if the radius does not fit in half of the edge.

The fillet follows tangent edges: one selected edge can round a whole loop (a rounded block: 1 edge selected, 8 faces made). The document state says so for every fillet: «selected_edges» is how many edges were selected, «faces» how many faces the fillet made. The answer carries «selected_edges» and «faces» too, read the same way.

I REFUSE IF the volume of the part does not change after the fillet is made: the feature is in the tree and worked nothing, and I say it is still there to undo. On a concave edge the volume grows, and that is fine. material_change_mm3 gives the change (after minus before); volume_not_read says when the volume could not be read.

edges_uid.description: identifiers of edges that ALREADY exist, taken from the document state

edges_ref.description:
the edges created by an earlier step of this same plan — for example «fillet the four corners of the plate you make at step 1». How many edges there are is known only inside SolidWorks. Give this OR edges_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- bottom_edges: the edges of the border at the bottom of the extrusion
- side_edges: the edges along the direction of extrusion, the vertical ones
- top_edges: the edges of the border at the top of the extrusion
- all_edges: all the edges created by that step

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

operations.name: circular_pattern
operations.summary: Repeats a feature in a circle around an axis or a straight edge.
operations.details:
Repeats a feature already made, in a circle around an axis. The feature and the axis are indicated with the identifiers taken from the document state.

THE AXIS CAN BE A STRAIGHT EDGE of the part — the ones the state lists as «E1», «E2» — or a reference axis already in the document.

To repeat around a HOLE you need an axis that passes through its centre: the edge of the hole is a circle, not a line, and it is refused as a direction. If that axis does not exist yet, make it first with «create_axis».

feature_uid.description: what to repeat, if it is already in the tree

feature_ref.description:
the feature made by an earlier step of this same plan — «make a hole and then repeat it 6 times». Give this OR feature_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- feature: the feature made by that step, to repeat it

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

axis_uid.description: around what: an axis already in the document, or a STRAIGHT edge of the part («E1», «E2»...) taken from the state

axis_ref.description:
the axis created by an earlier step of this same plan — «make the axis of the hole and then repeat the feature 6 times around it». Give this OR axis_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- axis: the axis created by the step, from the centre of a hole or a shaft

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

operations.name: linear_pattern
operations.summary: Repeats a feature in a row, or in a grid in two directions: eight holes in a row are made this way.
operations.details:
Repeats a feature already made, in a row along an axis — or in a grid, along two axes together. It is the twin of «circular_pattern» and is indicated the same way.

Eight holes in a row are made THIS WAY, not by calling the hole eight times with eight coordinates: the finished part declares that those holes are a series, and changing their pitch becomes a single dimension.

THE DIRECTION IS TAKEN FROM A STRAIGHT EDGE of the part: the ones the document state lists as «E1», «E2»... For a row along the plate you indicate the long edge; for a grid, two edges perpendicular to each other.

An axis made with «create_axis» also works, but that one is born from the centre of a hole and is perpendicular to the drilled face: it is for repeating INTO THE THICKNESS, almost never for a row.

«axis1_uid» is required. «axis2_uid» is only for a grid — a plate drilled in a matrix; for a single row omit it together with pitch2_mm and instance_count2.

The axis decides the direction, not a sign in the parameters: if the repeat comes out on the wrong side use «flip1».

I REFUSE IF THE DIRECTION COMES FROM A CURVED EDGE: a straight edge is needed. An arc does not have a single direction, and taking one at random would mean a crooked pattern that looks right.

feature_uid.description: what to repeat, if it is already in the tree

feature_ref.description:
the feature made by an earlier step of this plan. Give this OR feature_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- feature: the feature made by that step, to repeat it

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

axis1_uid.description: direction 1: a STRAIGHT edge of the part («E1», «E2»...) taken from the state, or an axis already in the document

axis1_ref.description:
direction 1, if the axis is created by an earlier step of this plan with «create_axis». One OR the other.

Allowed kinds:
- axis: the axis created by the step, from the centre of a hole or a shaft

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

instance_count1.description: how many copies in all, the original included

operations.name: fill_pattern
operations.summary: Fills a flat face with copies of a feature: a plate drilled for lightness, a vent grille.
operations.details:
Fills a flat face with copies of a feature that already exists: a plate drilled for lightness, a vent grille, a sieve. SOLIDWORKS puts the first copy at the CENTER of the face and adds concentric loops spaced «pitch_mm» apart, with «copies_per_turn» copies on each loop, as long as the face holds them; the ones that would fall outside the outline (shrunk by «margin_mm») are not made. The original stays where it was.

HOW MANY COPIES FIT IS DECIDED BY THE FACE, not by a number you give: the answer counts them in «copies_made». On a 100 x 60 plate with one Ø8 hole, a pitch of about 17 and 10 copies per loop, it is 14.

Three things are needed: the feature («feature_uid» or «feature_ref»), the boundary face it sits on («face_uid» or «face_ref») and a DIRECTION, that is, a straight edge that runs along the face («axis_uid», for example its long edge) or an axis that lies along that face («axis_ref»). The axis of a hole drilled into the face, as «create_axis» makes it, runs across the face and is refused. The direction orients the loops. Measured with an edge of the boundary face; an axis lying along the face is accepted, but no test has used one yet.

For copies in a row or in a grid use «linear_pattern»; for a circle of copies around an axis, «circular_pattern». The layout is circular only: the square, polygon and perforation layouts are not tested.

I REFUSE IF THE DIRECTION IS MISSING: without it SOLIDWORKS creates nothing and does not say why (measured, even though the guide calls it optional). I REFUSE IF THE BOUNDARY FACE IS NOT FLAT, and IF THE DIRECTION IS NOT IN THE PLANE OF THE FACE (an edge of the thickness). And I refuse, removing the pattern, if it comes out with features in error, with the bodies changed, or with copies that bite into the edge or merge with each other.

feature_uid.description: the feature to repeat, if it is already in the tree

feature_ref.description:
the feature made by an earlier step of this plan. Give this OR feature_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- feature: the feature made by that step, to repeat it

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

face_uid.description: the FLAT face to lay the copies out in, taken from the state («F1»...): usually the one the hole starts from

face_ref.description:
the face created by an earlier step of this same plan. Give this OR face_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- pocket_floor: the floor of the pocket (there only if the pocket is blind)
- bottom_face: the face on the sketch plane, the bottom of the extrusion
- top_face: the face on top of the extrusion, the one opposite the sketch plane

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

axis_uid.description: the direction of the loops: a STRAIGHT edge that runs along the boundary face («E1», «E2»...), for example its long edge, or an axis already in the document that lies along the face. Always needed: without it the pattern is not born

axis_ref.description:
the direction, when a previous step of this plan makes the axis with «create_axis»: only an axis that lies along the boundary face works (for example the axis of a shaft lying on it); the axis of a hole drilled into the face runs across it and is refused. One OR the other.

Allowed kinds:
- axis: the axis made by that step

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

pitch_mm.description: distance between one loop of copies and the next, center to center

copies_per_turn.description: how many copies on each loop around the center of the face

margin_mm.description: how far the copies stay from the edge of the face; default 0

operations.name: chamfer_edges
operations.summary: Chamfers one or more edges: deburring, an assembly lead-in, a weld bevel.
operations.details:
Chamfer on one or more edges. It is the twin of «fillet_edges» and the edges are given the same way.

The default is 45 degrees, by far the most common chamfer. For a non-symmetric chamfer — a weld bevel, a lead-in that has to enter a seat — give «second_leg_mm» and the angle is ignored.

Chamfer or fillet is not an aesthetic preference: a chamfer is made with a milling cutter or a file, a fillet needs a radius tool. If the user says «chamfer», do not make a fillet.

I REFUSE IF THE CHAMFER IS TOO BIG FOR THE EDGE -- not even half of it fits. A value over the limit does not always give an error: sometimes a degenerate geometry comes out that passes the rebuild.

The chamfer follows tangent edges like the fillet. The document state lists each chamfer with «selected_edges» and «faces», and its sizes by type: angle-distance «leg1_mm» + «angle_deg», distance-distance «leg1_mm» + «leg2_mm», and a vertex chamfer (made by hand) «vertex_distances_mm», its three distances along the corner's edges. The answer carries «selected_edges» and «faces» too, read the same way.

I REFUSE IF the volume of the part does not change after the chamfer is made: the feature is in the tree and worked nothing, and I say it is still there to undo. On a concave edge the volume grows, and that is fine. material_change_mm3 gives the change (after minus before); volume_not_read says when the volume could not be read.

edges_uid.description: edges that ALREADY exist, taken from the state

edges_ref.description:
the edges created by an earlier step of this plan. Give this OR edges_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- bottom_edges: the edges of the border at the bottom of the extrusion
- side_edges: the edges along the extrusion direction, the vertical ones
- top_edges: the edges of the border at the top of the extrusion
- all_edges: all the edges created by that step

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

leg_mm.description: how much material is removed, measured on one face

second_leg_mm.description: only for a non-symmetric chamfer: the leg on the other face

operations.name: mirror
operations.summary: Mirrors a feature across one of the three base planes.
operations.details:
Mirrors a feature that already exists across a plane of symmetry. The feature is given as for «circular_pattern».

The plane is always one of the three base planes, and it must be stated: getting it wrong does not move the geometry a little, it puts it somewhere else on the part, and the build succeeds all the same.

The FEATURE is mirrored, not the whole body: for a symmetric part, mirror the hole or pocket that is missing on one side.

I REFUSE IF THE PLANE DOES NOT EXIST, and I tell you which ones there are. Invented names -- «diagonal», «oblique» -- I do not interpret: mirroring across the wrong plane produces a plausible and wrong part.

feature_uid.description: what to mirror, if it is already in the tree

feature_ref.description:
the feature made by an earlier step of this plan. Give this OR feature_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- feature: the feature made by that step, to repeat it

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

operations.name: move_bodies
operations.summary: Moves or COPIES bodies that already exist, by a given distance.
operations.details:
Moves the given bodies by «dx_mm», «dy_mm», «dz_mm». With «copy» true it LEAVES THEM WHERE THEY ARE and puts copies further along: this is how two equal frames at a certain distance are made.

IT IS NEEDED WHEN THE PART HAS TWO EQUAL PARTS IN DIFFERENT PLACES. A rack made of two frames 600 mm apart is not asked for by making the frame twice: the second time would be refused, because the same operation twice with the same numbers makes two overlapping bodies. You make ONE frame, and then copy it moved 600 along Z.

Which bodies: «bodies_uid» for the ones that ALREADY exist in the document (C1, C2...), «bodies_ref» for the ones an earlier step of this same plan creates. One or the other, never both.

Straight-line move only: this operation does not rotate anything. If rotating is needed, say so instead of pretending.

bodies_uid.description: the bodies to move, by identifier from the document state (C1, C2...)

bodies_ref.description:
the bodies created by an earlier step of this same plan. Give this OR bodies_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- bodies: the bars created by that step, all together

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

copy.description: true: leaves the originals and adds moved copies. Default: false, that is, it just moves them.

copy_count.description: how many copies, only if «copy» is true. Default 1. Copy number k ends up at k times the move.

operations.name: cylindrical_cut
operations.summary: A round cut on a face: for a passage that is NOT a hole for a fastener.
operations.details:
Makes a hole on an existing face, at the given coordinates in the plane of that face. Through or blind.

I REFUSE IF THE HOLE FALLS ENTIRELY OUTSIDE THE MATERIAL (I tell you between which coordinates the face lies) and IF it is so wide that it covers the whole face: that is not a hole, it is a part that disappears.

face_ref.description:
the face created by an earlier step of this same plan, when the hole goes on geometry you are creating now and which therefore has no identifier yet. Give this OR face_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- pocket_floor: the floor of the pocket (there only if the pocket is blind)
- bottom_face: the face on the sketch plane, the bottom of the extrusion
- top_face: the face on top of the extrusion, the one opposite the sketch plane

They are the same numbers as the «point_mm» you read in the document state, so you can start from those. The third coordinate is not needed: it is the plane of the face.

WHAT KEEPS THE HOLE WHERE IT IS WHEN THE PART CHANGES. Without it, x_mm/y_mm are absolute coordinates: if the plate gets longer, the hole stays where it was. For EACH axis, «x» and «y», both required, one of two things: {"edge_uid": "E7", "distance_mm": 20}, the distance from the CENTER to a straight edge of the same face that runs along the other axis; or {"centered_between": ["E3", "E5"]}, halfway between two opposite edges. x_mm/y_mm stay required and must name the same point.

I also refuse when I cannot do those checks: relations of the sketch I cannot read, or an anchor dimension I cannot read or move (the test would pass without testing anything).

centered_between.description: two opposite edges of the face, from the state, that run along y_mm: the center stays halfway between them

distance_mm.description: from the CENTER of the profile to the edge, measured along y_mm

centered_between.description: two opposite edges of the face, from the state, that run along x_mm: the center stays halfway between them

through_all.description: default: yes, unless «depth_mm» is given: then the cut stops at that depth

depth_mm.description: the depth of a blind cut, in mm; given alone it makes the cut blind, and with «through_all» true it is not used

operations.details:

operations.name: apply_material
operations.summary: Assigns the material to the part: without it there is no weight and no usable cut list.
operations.details:
Assigns the material to the part. ALWAYS DO THIS, on every part you draw: without a material there is no density, without density there is no weight, and the cut list comes out with an empty material column — that is, it is no use for buying the steel.

Write the name as a designer would say it («S235JR», «AISI 304», «6061 Alloy»): the exact spelling is found by the workstation, which has the real libraries. If the name matches more than one material, or none, the operation fails and lists the ones that exist, and then you ask the user: between 1.0037 and 1.0116 you do not choose at random.

IF YOU DO NOT GIVE THE MATERIAL I use «S235JR», which is what this shop works with unless told otherwise, and I write it in the answer, so you know I chose it and you did not.

The material goes on EVERY configuration of the part, each one set and read back by its own name (measured: the empty configuration name reaches only the active configuration and the ones derived from it). The answer lists them in «configurations»; I refuse the step, naming them, if any configuration does not take the material.

material.description: for example «S235JR», «AISI 304», «6061 Alloy». If you do not give it I use S235JR, and I write that in the answer.

library.description: optional: the name of the library, if you know which one to search. Leave it alone if you do not.

operations.name: create_axis
operations.summary: An axis along the centre of a hole or a shaft: it is for repeating AROUND that hole.
operations.details:
Creates a reference axis along the centre of an existing cylindrical or conical face — the hole or shaft around which you then repeat something with «circular_pattern».

WHEN IT IS REALLY NEEDED: to repeat around a HOLE. The edge of a hole is a circle, not a straight line, and it is rejected as a direction; the axis, instead, passes through its centre.

WHEN IT IS NOT NEEDED: for a row or a grid. There the direction is taken from a straight edge of the part, which is already in the state («E1», «E2»...). The axis of a hole points INTO THE THICKNESS of the plate: repeating along that does not make a row.

Cylindrical or conical faces only: a planar face has no axis. In the document state they are the ones with «planar: false».

On a sheet-metal part too: the axis is the one the call made, wherever SOLIDWORKS puts it in the tree (before the flat pattern).

face_uid.description: the cylindrical or conical face, taken from the document state

face_ref.description:
the face created by an earlier step of this plan. Give this OR face_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- pocket_floor: the floor of the pocket (it exists only if the pocket is blind)
- bottom_face: the face on the sketch plane, the bottom of the extrusion
- top_face: the face at the top of the extrusion, the one opposite the sketch plane

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

operations.name: create_plane
operations.summary: A new reference plane, parallel to a base plane and offset by a distance.
operations.details:
Creates a reference plane parallel to a base plane (front, top or right) and offset by a distance along its normal. The base plane is found by its geometry (its normal through the origin), not by its place in the tree, so a template with an extra plane before the three default ones does not move it. It is for building a sketch at a certain height or depth without touching the base plane — «a plane parallel to top, at 600 mm» to work at half the height of an upright.

Negative distance: on the opposite side. Zero distance: a plane coincident with the base, as a separate object.

Base planes only: this version cannot rest the new plane on a face of the part.

plane.description: base plane: front, top or right

distance_mm.description: how far it is offset from the base plane. Negative for the other direction.

operations.name: weld_bead
operations.summary: Cosmetic weld bead between two faces of two bars that meet at an angle.
operations.details:
Puts a cosmetic fillet weld bead between TWO faces of two bodies that touch along an edge and form an angle: for one bar butted against another, the SIDE face of the bar and the face it arrives on. It neither removes nor adds material: it documents the weld, and it ends up in the drawings and in the bill of materials.

ONE PAIR OF FACES PER CALL. A bead that runs all round a rectangular tube is several calls, one per side: with more than one face per side SOLIDWORKS creates nothing. The faces are given by identifier, taken from the document state: this is an operation you ask for AFTER the bars and the cuts are made, by looking at them.

I REFUSE IF the two faces do not touch, or are parallel: SOLIDWORKS would create the bead all the same, and the bill of materials would end up with a weld that does not exist. The length I return is that of the edge they have in common.

start_face_uid.description: a face of the first body, taken from the document state (F1, F2...)

end_face_uid.description: a face of the OTHER body, which touches the first one along an edge and makes an angle with it

operations.name: cut_list
operations.summary: Creates or updates the cut list of the weldment part. Goes last.
operations.details:
Creates or updates the CUT LIST of the weldment part: the list of bars with profile, size, length and quantity.

It is the document you take to the workshop, and it is the reason a frame is made with structural members instead of extrusions. Call it AFTER you have placed all the bars and made all the cuts: a cut list calculated earlier reports lengths that change afterwards.

ONE ITEM FOR EACH GROUP OF IDENTICAL BARS: the part becomes a weldment (the «Weldment» feature, named in the language of the installation, if it is missing) and the cut list is the automatic one of SOLIDWORKS, which separates the bars by length. The answer carries the items (description, length, quantity), and the sum of the quantities must be the number of bars, otherwise it says so. The gussets and the end caps are in the list too, one item for each group of identical ones: they have no description and no length, so every item says its item_type (weldment_member, solid_body or sheet_metal) and names its first_body.

The answer says what SOLIDWORKS answered: automatic_cut_list_set (null when the cut list was automatic already), automatic_update_set and cut_list_updated. When the cut list did not update, the warning field of the answer says the numbers may be stale. Each item gets bodies_equal, and the same warning field speaks when an item QUANTITY differs from the bodies of its folder, when one item holds bodies of different volume, or when the folders hold a different number of bodies than the part. A cut list that is not automatic (made by hand or before library 0.124.0) is refused: delete it first. When a refusal removes the weldment feature this step added, the message says whether IsWeldment reads false again.

update_if_exists.description: if the cut list already exists, it recalculates it instead of creating a second one (default: yes)

operations.name: gusset
operations.summary: Reinforcing gusset, triangular or polygonal, in the corner between two planar faces of two bars that meet.
operations.details:
Puts a reinforcing GUSSET in the corner between two bars of a welded frame: a plate, a body of its own, that stiffens the joint and ends up in the cut list.

THE TWO FACES are given by identifier, taken from the document state: this is an operation you ask for AFTER the bars and the cuts are made, by looking at them. They must be PLANAR, make an angle and touch along an edge: for one bar butted against another, the SIDE face of the bar and the face it arrives on (the same ones as for «weld_bead»). At a corner of rectangular tubes there are four candidate faces, and picking two «likely» ones would mean putting the reinforcement on the wrong side. Parallel, distant or curved faces: I refuse, before touching the part.

THE PROFILE: «triangular» (the default) with the two sides «leg1_mm» and «leg2_mm» along the two faces; or «polygonal», which cuts off the tip and also needs the two short sides «side3_mm» and «side4_mm», shorter than the two legs. A polygon without short sides is degenerate and I refuse it: it is the defect because of which this operation never created anything until library 0.139.0. The thickness lies on both sides of the gusset's plane; «position» is «start», «center» (the default) or «end» along the common edge, and I refuse any other value instead of quietly putting it in the center.

THE ANSWER IS READ BACK, not repeated: the added volume against the hand calculation («volume_added_mm3», «volume_expected_mm3»), the bodies before and after, the thickness, the profile, the position and the two supporting faces read back from the feature («thickness_read_mm», «profile_read», «location_read», «supporting_faces_area_mm2»), the new body and its box («new_body», «new_body_box_mm»). If one of these does not match, I remove the gusset and tell you. If you only need to document the weld, use «weld_bead».

faces_uid.description: exactly TWO planar faces, one per bar, that touch along an edge and make an angle, taken from the document state (F1, F2...)

thickness_mm.description: thickness of the plate, on both sides of its plane

leg1_mm.description: one of the two sides of the gusset, the ones that run along the two faces. Which side goes on which face the guide does not say, and no test has told them apart (measured only with equal sides): if it matters to you, look at the part afterwards

leg2_mm.description: the other side, along the other face (see leg1_mm)

profile.description: shape of the plate (default: triangular). The polygonal one cuts off the tip and needs «side3_mm» and «side4_mm»

side3_mm.description: only with the polygonal profile: first short side, shorter than the two legs

side4_mm.description: only with the polygonal profile: second short side, shorter than the two legs

position.description: where it sits along the edge between the two faces (default: center)

operations.name: structural_member
operations.summary: Real metalwork bars along the segments you give: this is what generates the cut list.
operations.details:
Creates one or more BARS of a welded frame: real structural members, with the profile taken from the company library.

IT IS THE OPERATION TO USE FOR EVERYTHING THAT IS METALWORK: tubes, angles, flat bars, IPE, HEA, HEB, UPN, UPE, U and T sections — whether a single bar or a whole frame.

Why extruding a section is not enough: only the structural member generates the CUT LIST, carries the name of the profile, and can be mitered at 45 degrees at the joints. An extruded bar has the same shape and is no use for making the part.

FIRST CALL «weldment_profiles» and copy «profile_path» and «configuration» from there to the letter. Do not compose the name of the size: the library is not uniform and an invented name makes SolidWorks use another size, without an error.

The segments are the lines along which the bars run, in model coordinates in mm. A straight bar 200 long on the X axis is one segment only: from [0,0,0] to [200,0,0]. A rectangular frame is four segments that close.

If the weldment profile library is still open and modified in SOLIDWORKS after the insertion, the answer carries «profile_library_warning»: close that library without saving, or a Ctrl+S would rewrite the shared library. The warning can carry a second sentence: the library is still LOADED, hidden (an open document references it, or the close did nothing), with the insertion's changes in memory even if its save flag reads clean.

I REFUSE IF «configuration» is empty and the profile file has several sizes, and I list them: with an empty size SOLIDWORKS builds the size the file was saved on (measured: the 20 x 20 of the four in iso\square tube.sldlfp). An empty size is accepted only on a file with one size, and the answer says so in «configuration_note».

profile_path.description: full path of the .sldlfp, copied from weldment_profiles

configuration.description: the size, copied TO THE LETTER from weldment_profiles (e.g. «80X80X5»: upper case and commas included). Empty only for a profile file with one size.

segments.description: the lines along which the bars run, in mm in model coordinates

start.description: [x, y, z] of the start, in mm

end.description: [x, y, z] of the end, in mm

rotation_deg.description: rotation of the profile about its own axis (default: 0). Needed when an angle or a U has to be turned.

corner_treatment.description:
how the bars of THIS group meet each other, WHERE THEY TOUCH. «miter» is the 45 degree cut at the corners (default: miter, the 45 degree miter, wherever the bars of this group touch, closed or open path; the answer says it was the default in «corner_treatment_note»); «butt1»/«butt2» is one bar butted against the other; «none» leaves them interpenetrating and should be said only if you really want that.

It does NOT cut the FREE ends. On a single bar, or at the two ends of an open frame, there is nothing to cut against and this parameter has no effect.

gap_mm.description: gap between the bars at the joints, for the weld bead (default: 0)

operations.name: trim_members
operations.summary: Trims or extends the bars where they meet.
operations.details:
Trims the bars where they meet, or extends them until they touch. It is the «trim/extend» of the weldments toolbar.

Needed when two groups of bars cross and have not been treated at the corners: without it the bodies stay interpenetrating and the cut list reports lengths that do not match in the workshop.

I return how much the volume changed (negative = removed). I REFUSE IF the part does not change: that means the bars do not meet, and I do not confirm a cut that cuts nothing.

A bar that stops short of the other one is extended to its face (measured: a bar 20 mm short grows by 20 mm, Options 1|2|8); a bar that enters the other is cut at its face as before. The coped cut is not used.

bodies_to_trim_uid.description: the bars to trim or extend (a bar that stops short grows to the other one), by the identifier of the document state (C1, C2...). Use this for bodies that exist ALREADY; the other field for bodies a previous step of this plan creates. One or the other, never both.

bodies_to_trim_ref.description:
the bars to trim or extend, made by a previous step

Kinds allowed:
- bodies: the bars created by that step, all together

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

trim_boundary_uid.description: the bars to cut against, by identifier taken from the document state (C1, C2...). Use this for bodies that ALREADY exist; the other field is for bodies that a previous step of this plan creates. One or the other, never both.

trim_boundary_ref.description:
the bars to cut against, from a previous step

Kinds allowed:
- bodies: the bars created by that step, all together

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

end_condition.description: how the cut ends (default: cut). Any other word is refused before the part is touched, a word meaning no corner included: the trim/extend has no such corner type, and none was measured. The answer names the condition used in end_condition.

gap_mm.description: gap left (default: 0). The gap you pass is always the one applied, even 0: the last gap given by hand in SOLIDWORKS is not inherited

operations.name: end_cap
operations.summary: Closes the open ends of hollow bars with a cap.
operations.details:
Closes the open ends of a hollow bar with a cap. It goes on the end faces created by a previous step, or on the bars that are already in the document («C1», «C2»...).

THE ONLY THING THAT MAY BE MISSING IS THE THICKNESS OF THE CAP. It has no default, because it is a design choice: ask for it, and ask ONLY for that. The material is not needed — it is applied afterwards with its own operation, and it does not change the shape of the cap.

A PLANAR FACE WITH A HOLE MACHINED INTO IT IS NOT AN OPEN END. A drilled side wall of a tube (its outer and its inner face) is looked at and left out, and the answer counts it in machined_faces_skipped. An open end is a face whose void was made by the bar itself, so an end whose inner edges were chamfered or counterbored is left out the same way. When a face cannot be told apart, nothing is capped and the answer says why.

bodies_uid.description: the bars whose open ends are to be capped, by identifier taken from the document state (C1, C2...). Use this for bodies that ALREADY exist; the other field is for bodies that a previous step of this plan creates. One or the other, never both.

ends_ref.description:
the end faces to cap, from a previous step

Kinds allowed:
- free_ends: the end faces of the bars of that step that are still open, the ones that get capped (a wall with a hole machined into it is not an end: it is left out)

step.description: the sequence number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be a step BEFORE this one.

inset_mm.description: NOT a depth: the side gap between the cap and the inside of the tube wall, on every side. The cap always sits flush with the end of the bar. 0 or absent: half the wall thickness per side (measured on an 80 x 80 x 5 tube, 70 x 70 inside: 65 x 65 caps); a value above 0 is that gap. A cap that fills the whole inside with no gap cannot be asked for yet.

chamfer_mm.description: IGNORED today: the corner treatment of the cap is off, and without it SOLIDWORKS drops the chamfer (measured: 2 mm gives the same volume as none). The cap corners stay sharp whatever the value.

operations.name: rectangular_frame
operations.summary: A rectangular frame of four bars, given with two dimensions instead of eight coordinates.
operations.details:
RECIPE: a flat rectangular frame, four bars welded at the corners. It is the most common case of metalwork, and it is asked for with two dimensions instead of eight coordinates.

The dimensions are the OVERALL OUTSIDE SIZE of the finished frame. The plane says which principal plane it lies on.

As for «structural_member», the profile and the size are copied from «weldment_profiles».

I REFUSE IF the profile does not fit in the two sizes (its overhang, measured on a trial frame, is as large as a side), or if «measured_as» is neither «overall» nor «center_distance» (upper or lower case does not matter), and I draw nothing. The answer says which reading it used («measured_as»), whether the profile's overhang was measured now or remembered from an earlier frame («overhang_source»: «measured» or «archive»), and, if the weldment profile library is still open and modified in SOLIDWORKS afterwards, «profile_library_warning»: close that library without saving. The warning or the refusal can also say that the library is still LOADED, hidden, because an open document references it or the close did nothing, with the changes in memory even if its save flag reads clean.

configuration.description: the profile size, copied from weldment_profiles. Empty is accepted only on a profile file with one size; with several sizes it is refused, and the sizes are listed.

plane.description: construction plane: front, top or right

corner_treatment.description: default: miter (45 degree miter); the answer says when it was the default («corner_treatment_note»)

measured_as.description: what the two dimensions mean: «overall» is the size of the finished part from outside to outside (it is what a designer means by «frame 1000x800»); «center_distance» is the distance between the axes of the bars. Default: overall. Upper or lower case does not matter («Overall» is «overall»); any other word is refused.

centered.description: frame centered on the origin (default: yes)

operations.name: create_drawing
operations.summary: Opens a new drawing of the part you are looking at.
operations.details:
Creates the DRAWING document of the open part and brings it to the front. The part stays open: a drawing view attaches to the PATH of an open document, not to a file.

THE PART MUST ALREADY BE SAVED. If it is not, save it first with «save_document».

The drawing template is NOT chosen: the one of this installation is used, which carries the shop's title block and the right projection angle. From here on the active document is the DRAWING, and the operations that model the part no longer apply until you go back to the part.

paper_size.description: sheet size; A3 if you say nothing

operations.precondition: a part or an assembly SAVED to disk

operations.name: export_pdf
operations.summary: The PDF of ALL the sheets, with the pages counted.
operations.details:
Writes the PDF of the drawing.

ALL the sheets, not only the one you are looking at: the standard export takes the current sheet, and a three-sheet drawing reaches the shop as a single page without any error. After writing the file the pages are COUNTED and compared with the sheets: if they do not match, I tell you.

I REFUSE IF SOLIDWORKS does not accept the request for every sheet (IExportPdfData.SetSheets answers false), before writing anything; and when the pages of the written file cannot be counted, saying where the file is: without that count, the check this operation exists for did not run.

The answer carries save_warnings (the swFileSaveWarning_e names, or «none») and save_warnings_note when the drawing needed a rebuild, had rebuild errors, or had views needing an update. A failed save gives the error and warning names next to the raw codes.

With «search» the PDF is READ BACK: tell me the texts that must be there (the drawing number, the part name) and I tell you which are there («found») and which are not («not_found»). The text in the PDF is written as glyph indices, and a search in the bytes does not find it: here it is decoded.

path.description: where to write the PDF. If you do not say, next to the drawing, with the same name.

search.description: texts the PDF must contain: the file is read back and I say which ones are there

operations.name: set_sheet
operations.summary: Sheet size and scale.
operations.details:
Changes the SIZE and the SCALE of the active sheet, and reads back to check.

THE PROJECTION ANGLE IS NOT TOUCHED and is not a parameter. A drawing in third-angle projection has the right and left views swapped, gives no error, and the part that comes out of it is mirrored: what the shop's drawing template has already decided is read and written back unchanged. You find which one it is in the measurements.

scale_numerator.description: the first number of the scale: the 1 in «1:2»

scale_denominator.description: the second number of the scale: the 2 in «1:2»

operations.name: model_dimensions
operations.summary: Brings onto the drawing the dimensions the part already has.
operations.details:
Takes the dimensions from the MODEL and puts them on the views.

The import works from this bridge, out of process: measured on 26/9/2026 (7 dimensions on a plate) and again on 28/9/2026. To put on the drawing a dimension the model does not have, «drawing_dimension» CREATES it on the edges the view shows.

Each model dimension comes in once: I ask SOLIDWORKS to eliminate duplicates (DuplicateDims true), so a dimension already shown in one view is not repeated in another (measured: 4 dimensions on a plate that got 7 before).

Why it exists all the same: a dimension that comes from the model cannot carry a number different from the geometry, while the SolidWorks API lets you write on the drawing a text the geometry does not have.

By default only the dimensions MARKED for the drawing come in, that is, the ones chosen to be shown: with «all_dimensions» the others come in too, and the drawing becomes quite a lot denser.
