By default only the dimensions MARKED for drawing come in, fallbacks included. If the part has dimensions and none is marked, I refuse and say so: pass all_dimensions=true to import them all, or mark on the model the ones the drawing must show.

I REFUSE IF the drawing has no views (the dimensions would have nothing to attach to) and if no dimension comes in: I tell you, with how many the part has marked, instead of answering «done».

all_dimensions.description: also the dimensions not marked for the drawing. It makes the drawing denser: use it when the marked ones are not enough. Without it, a part where no dimension is marked for drawing is refused, not imported.

hole_callouts.description: also the annotations of Hole Wizard holes (M8, depth, thread). On if you say nothing.

operations.precondition: a drawing with at least one view

operations.name: center_marks
operations.summary: Checks that every hole in the views has its center mark, really counting them, and refuses if one is missing.
operations.details:
CHECKS that every hole visible in the views has its center mark, and tries to add it where it is missing. SOLIDWORKS puts them in by itself when it creates the view, if the document option that puts center marks on the holes of a new view (Detailing, automatic insertion on view creation) is on: those holes I recognise («circles_already_marked»). A new mark cannot be made from code (measured): a hole without a mark is a refusal, with the way out — the option on and the view rebuilt.

WHY IT IS NEEDED. A drawing with twelve holes and no center mark prints and looks complete. In the shop, the thing needed to drill is missing: **where the centre is.**

I TELL YOU HOW MANY WERE BORN, counted on the view: every mark must raise the count by one, and a circle left without a mark is a refusal. If the number is **zero** I tell you instead of saying «done» — almost always the view is the wrong one (holes seen as circles are seen from above, usually V2).

THE SIZE, if you do not tell me, is the document's: it is a house convention.

Without «view» I look at all of them. Not fillets or slots: measured, on arcs the mark is not born from code.

CENTER MARKS ARE COUNTED BY ENUMERATING THEM: the SOLIDWORKS counter (GetCenterMarkCount) does not see the ones put in when the view is created, and said zero on a sheet that had three.

The walk over the holes is the one standard_views also uses on views left with no mark.

view.description: ONE view, as the state of the drawing calls it (V1, V2...) or by name. Empty = all the views.

applies_to.description: «holes», the whole circles (the only value accepted: «fillets» is refused, because on a fillet arc the mark is not born from code, measured).

size_mm.description: how big the mark is. If you do not say, I use the document's settings, which is almost always the right thing.

extended_lines.description: the axis lines that go out from the mark to the edge of the circle. Off if you say nothing.

operations.precondition: a drawing with at least one view

operations.name: drawing_dimension
operations.summary: Puts dimensions on the edges of a view, and READS BACK how much they measure.
operations.details:
Puts reference dimensions on the edges of a drawing view, and for each one tells you **how many millimetres it measures**, read back from SOLIDWORKS after placing it.

THIS IS THE OPERATION THAT DIMENSIONS. «model_dimensions» does something else: it IMPORTS the dimensions the part already has, and on this installation it brings in none (measured on eight different drawing templates). If you need a dimensioned drawing, use this one.

THE EDGES HAVE A NUMBER, and I give it to you: the view exposes its list, and without «edges» I dimension the first «count». Ask me for an edge that does not exist and I answer how many the view has, instead of dimensioning another one.

I TELL YOU HOW MANY WERE BORN, not that I called the API: the dimensions are counted before and after, one by one. If none is born I tell you, and I tell you which edges I tried.

WHERE THEY END UP: outside the view — the horizontal ones below, the vertical ones at the side, inside the sheet frame — from the smallest to the largest.

OVERLAPS ARE CHECKED AND REPORTED, not avoided: the true rectangle of every dimension text, read back from SOLIDWORKS, against the other texts of the whole drawing and against the lines of the part in this view. «overlapping_texts» lists each overlap, and the answer also gives their count and how many texts were read; null, not 0, means the texts could not be read, or the walk over the dimensions of the drawing broke off before the end, so overlaps are unknown. Dimension lines, extension lines and the title block are not checked. The dimensions are correct; a well laid out drawing is still a trade.

I DIMENSION HOLES AND CHAMFERS BY MYSELF, in every view that shows them, even if you do not ask: holes with the HOLE CALLOUT («4× Ø8 THRU», with the word for «through» that SOLIDWORKS writes in the language of the installation, one callout per diameter AND depth: two through Ø8 and two blind Ø8 get two callouts, never one «4×») and the position from the two reference edges, the left one and the bottom one; chamfers with the CHAMFER DIMENSION («5 x 45°»), not with their edges — the hypotenuse and the segments shortened by the chamfer are not dimensioned. A blind hole carries the depth («Ø8 ↧5»); if the callout is not born, I write it myself from the geometry.

THE «4×» IS READ BACK: after writing the count in front of the callout I read its prefix again (holes[].prefix_read). If the count did not stick, the holes are listed in edges_not_dimensioned and the count must be written by hand; «how_many» is the number of holes, not the text.

A CIRCLE IS NOT ALWAYS A HOLE: the outline of a round part seen from the front has a diameter dimension (outer_diameters).

A ROUND PART SEEN FROM THE SIDE (shaft, bushing, pin) I dimension like this: the LENGTHS between faces, in parallel from the face of one end (round_lengths_mm), and the DIAMETERS from the two generatrices of each cylinder, with the Ø (round_diameters_mm), each one read back. SOLIDWORKS does not always expose the generatrices of a cylinder: those diameters I tell you in round_diameters_not_reached, and they must be dimensioned by hand (an internal hole is dimensioned from the view in which it is a circle).

ONLY ONE DIMENSION PER FEATURE ON THE WHOLE DRAWING: if the same extent of the part is already dimensioned in another view, here I skip it and tell you (UNI ISO 129-1). So dimension the views one at a time, and do not expect in each view the measurements another one already has.

ON EVERY SHEET: «already dimensioned» is read from the views of all the sheets, only from views of the same part and configuration, and a dimension hidden by hand does not count (one on a hidden layer, or of a suppressed feature, still does: I cannot see those). The answer says what was read: already_dimensioned_read_from («every sheet», or «current sheet only» when the drawing did not hand over its sheets), hidden_dimensions_not_counted, views_of_other_models_not_counted.

A DIMENSION BORN WITHOUT ITS OBJECT (the count of dimensions went up, the call returned nothing) stays: it is listed with its values null and named in edges_not_dimensioned, since its value was not read back. For a hole it does not trigger the fallback diameter dimension, which would be a second annotation on the same hole. The same holds in the turned view: a length or a diameter born without its object is not in round_lengths_mm or round_diameters_mm (they list what was read back), is not dimensioned again in another view and is not reported as not reached; one born between two silhouette edges without a face cannot be matched to a cylinder, so no further pair is tried, and its line in edges_not_dimensioned says so.

I REFUSE IF THE EDGE ASKED FOR DOES NOT EXIST in the view, and I tell you how many it shows. An index that is not there is the easiest mistake to make when dimensioning blind. And I refuse a view where nothing is left to dimension because everything is already dimensioned elsewhere: zero dimensions are not an answer of «done».

view.description: ONE view: its identifier in the state of the drawing (V1, V2...) or its name. Empty = the first real view.

edges.description: the numbers of the edges to dimension, from the list the view exposes (the first is 0). Empty = the first «count».

count.description: how many dimensions to put when you do not say which edges. Default 4.

offset_mm.description: how far below the extent of the view to put the first dimension. Default 12.

pitch_mm.description: the distance between one dimension and the next. Default 10.

operations.precondition: a drawing with at least one view that shows edges

operations.name: hole_table
operations.summary: The hole table on a view: a tag per hole, the position from the origin and the size.
operations.details:
Puts on the drawing the HOLE TABLE of the drilled face seen in a view: for each hole a tag (A1, A2...), the X and Y position from a corner vertex of the part, and the size («Ø8», with the depth or the word for «through» as SOLIDWORKS writes it). It is the table needed by whoever drills a plate with many holes, in place of one dimension per hole.

The view is the one in which the holes are seen as circles (usually V2, from above): the operation chooses the face among those that look toward the reader, the one with the most holes. «origin» says from which corner of that face it is measured (default bottom_left).

The table is READ BACK: the rows must be the holes plus the header, and every position written must correspond to a hole of the part measured on the view. Measured: with the origin and the face badly selected SOLIDWORKS produces an EMPTY table without an error.

I REFUSE IF no face with holes looks toward the reader in that view, and if the table is born empty or states positions the part does not have: in those cases I remove it.

view.description: the view, as the state of the drawing calls it (V1, V2...) or by name. Default the first.

origin.description: from which corner of the drilled face the positions are measured. Default bottom_left.

x_mm.description: where the top-left corner of the table goes on the sheet, in mm. Default 15.

y_mm.description: same, vertically. Default 15 below the top edge of the sheet.

tag_start.description: the letter of the tags. Default «A».

operations.precondition: a drawing with a view of the part in which the holes are seen as circles

operations.name: flat_pattern_view
operations.summary: The FLAT PATTERN view of a sheet-metal part on the drawing, measured against the part.
operations.details:
Puts on the drawing the FLAT PATTERN view of a sheet-metal part: the sheet laid flat, with the bend lines, as it is before going to the press. It is the view needed by whoever cuts the sheet.

The view is MEASURED. The overall size is read from the visible edges (not from the outline of the view, which includes the bend note and a margin — measured: 92.6 mm for a flat pattern of 80.7) and is compared with the flat pattern of the part measured before placing the view. The answer carries the overall size, the bend lines and the length of the flat pattern. The view goes in a free spot of the sheet (measured at scale 2:1 at 300/90 mm it fell in the title block).

I REFUSE IF the part is not sheet metal, if the view is born but is not a flat pattern, or if it measures something other than the flat pattern of the part: in those cases I remove it, and say so only after reading the views of the drawing again; if it is still there, I ask you to remove it. I also refuse, before placing any view, when the flat pattern of the part does not unsuppress (or suppress again) while I measure its flat length: the part may then be left flattened, and the message says so.

model.description: the path of the sheet-metal part. Empty = the one of the drawing.

configuration.description: the configuration of the part. Empty = the active one.

x_mm.description: where the centre of the view goes on the sheet, in mm. Empty = a free spot outside the views and the title block.

hide_bends.description: without the bend lines. Default false: whoever bends wants them.

operations.precondition: a drawing and, open, a sheet-metal part saved to disk

operations.name: drawing_weld_symbol
operations.summary: The ISO weld symbol on the joint between two bodies, in a view.
operations.details:
Puts on the drawing the WELD SYMBOL (ISO 2553) on the joint between two bodies of a weldment: the arrow on the joint line, the bead symbol (fillet, V, half V, butt), the throat «a» on the left and, if you give it, the length on the right.

I FIND THE JOINT MYSELF: among the edges the view shows, the one where one body touches the other (the longest). The symbol is moved out of the part, on the side of «side», beyond the dimensions already placed.

IT IS READ BACK: symbol, throat, length, «all around». The count of its texts is checked too: a code the library does not draw leaves one text (the throat) instead of two, and that symbol is refused. The code of the symbol is the one of the SOLIDWORKS library («<WELD-FILL>» for the fillet): measured, with a wrong code the symbol is born all the same, reads back the same, and does not draw the triangle.

I REFUSE IF the part has only one body, if no joint is seen in the view, and if the symbol born is not the one asked for (in that case I remove it, and say so only after counting the weld symbols of the drawing again).

view.description: the view, as the state of the drawing calls it (V1, V2...) or by name. Default the first.

throat_mm.description: the throat of the bead in mm (ISO 2553, «a»). From 0 to 50.

length_mm.description: the length of the bead, to the right of the symbol. Empty = the whole joint.

all_around.description: the all-around circle of the bead. Default false.

field_weld.description: the flag of the weld made in the field (on site). Default false.

both_sides.description: the bead on both sides of the joint. Default false.

side.description: on which side of the view the symbol goes. Default top.

operations.precondition: a drawing with a view of a weldment in which the joint between two bodies is seen

operations.name: drawing_bom
operations.summary: The BOM of an assembly on the drawing, compared with the components of the assembly.
operations.details:
Puts on the drawing the BOM of the assembly behind a view: item number, component, quantity. By default the first level; «parts_only» or «indented» for the others.

I COMPARE IT: the assembly knows by itself which components it has and how many; the items and the sum of the quantities must match. If they do not match I remove it and tell you.

Then I measure it and put it in a free spot of the sheet, outside the views and the title block.

I REFUSE IF there is no assembly behind the view (for a weldment there is «drawing_cut_list») or if there is no room on the sheet.

The count on the assembly side follows how each sub-assembly shows its children in the BOM (ChildComponentDisplayInBOM): in a top-level table a sub-assembly that promotes its children is replaced by them; in a parts-only table a sub-assembly that hides its children is one item. The indented table is compared with the rows of the assembly tree, as SOLIDWORKS writes them (measured): siblings with the same file and configuration make one row with their count; under a sub-assembly row stand the children of ONE instance, one level deeper (a sub-assembly used 3 times with 2 B inside: its row says 3, the B row under it says 2); a sub-assembly that hides its children is one row with nothing under it, and one that promotes them has no row and its children stand at its level. «counted_as» in the answer says how the expected items were counted.

A LIGHTWEIGHT SUB-ASSEMBLY REFUSES: how it shows its children in a BOM is in its document, which is not loaded; resolve it and ask again. A component is suppressed by its load state (GetSuppression2: IsSuppressed answers true on a lightweight component, measured), and a sub-assembly is recognised by its file extension, so a lightweight one is not taken for a part. A component whose load state cannot be read refuses the step.

IN WHICH CONFIGURATION: the table is made for the configuration the view shows, and the assembly is read in that same one. When the assembly has another configuration active, I activate the view's for the reading and put the active one back, reading it again: the answer gives the view's configuration and «assembly_active_configuration», the active one after the reading. If the view's configuration cannot be activated, or the active one cannot be put back, I refuse before inserting the table and say where the assembly stayed. The exclusion from the BOM is read in the configuration of the assembly that holds each component.

view.description: the view of the assembly (V1, V2...) or by name. Default the first.

template.description: the table template. Empty = the first one in the folder of the BOM templates.

operations.precondition: a drawing with a view of a saved assembly

operations.name: balloons
operations.summary: Ballooning: the balloons with the BOM item numbers on the components of a view, counted.
operations.details:
Does the BALLOONING: puts the balloons on the components of the assembly in a view, with the BOM item number (AutoBalloon5). It counts them on the view before and after, and tells you the numbers written. Then it compares the items of the BOM with the balloons of the WHOLE drawing and tells you which items are left without one (that component is not seen in this view: balloon another view). If every item already has its balloon elsewhere, it adds none and answers «nothing to add in this view».

I REFUSE IF there is no BOM on the drawing yet (ballooning carries its item number: put it first with «drawing_bom») or if there is no assembly behind the view.

If the view cannot be selected, the step is refused before AutoBalloon5 runs. balloons_returned is the number of notes AutoBalloon5 returned (null when it returned no array), and balloons_count_note appears when it disagrees with the count in the view.

view.description: the view (V1, V2...) or by name. Default the first.

layout.description: how to arrange the balloons around the view. Default square.

operations.precondition: a drawing with the BOM and a view of the assembly

operations.name: surface_finish
operations.summary: The surface roughness symbol (Ra in micrometres) on an outline edge of a view.
operations.details:
Puts the ROUGHNESS symbol (UNI EN ISO 1302) with its leader line on the outline edge of a view, from the «side» asked for, and moves it outside the part. «process»: material removal (the bar, default), any, no_removal (the little circle).

The Ra is READ BACK from the symbol. Measured: without moving it, SOLIDWORKS puts the symbol outside the frame, ignoring the coordinates; for this reason the position is set and read back.

I REFUSE IF Ra is not between 0 and 100 micrometres, if the view has no straight edge on that side, and if the symbol born says a different Ra.

view.description: the view, V1, V2... or by name. Default the first.

side.description: on which side of the view the edge it attaches to is. Default «top».

ra_um.description: the Ra roughness in micrometres, for example 3.2

process.description: how the surface is obtained. Default «material_removal».

operations.name: datum
operations.summary: A datum (A, B...) on an outline edge of a view.
operations.details:
Puts a DATUM (UNI EN ISO 5459): the triangle on the outline edge of the view from the «side» asked for, and the flag with the «letter» outside the part, on the same side. It is the reference that geometric tolerances cite.

The letter is READ BACK. Measured: left where it is born, SOLIDWORKS puts the flag on the other side of the edge and the line crosses the part; for this reason it is moved.

I REFUSE IF the letter is already on the drawing — two datums with the same letter give no error and make every tolerance ambiguous — and if the view has no straight edge on that side.

view.description: the view, V1, V2... or by name. Default the first.

side.description: on which side of the view the edge it attaches to is. Default «bottom».

letter.description: the letter of the datum, from A to Z. Default «A».

operations.name: geometric_tolerance
operations.summary: A geometric tolerance frame (flatness, perpendicularity, position...) on an edge.
operations.details:
Puts a GEOMETRIC TOLERANCE FRAME (UNI EN ISO 1101) with the arrow on the outline edge of the view from the «side» asked for: the «characteristic», the width of the zone in mm and the «references» (up to three datum letters, in the order primary, secondary, tertiary). «diameter» puts the Ø before the value (a cylindrical zone, for the position of an axis).

Symbol, value and references are READ BACK from the frame, and so does the Ø (diameter_read, from IGtol.GetFrameDiameterSymbols).

I REFUSE IF a form tolerance (straightness, flatness, circularity, cylindricity) cites a datum, if an orientation or position one cites none, if a cited datum is not on the drawing (put it first with «datum»), and if the frame born does not say what was asked for, Ø included: such a frame, or one that cannot be filled, is removed from the sheet, and said removed only after the frames of the drawing are counted again.

view.description: the view, V1, V2... or by name. Default the first.

side.description: on which side of the view the edge it attaches to is. Default «right».

value_mm.description: the width of the tolerance zone, in mm

references.description: the datum letters, up to three, in the order primary, secondary, tertiary

diameter.description: cylindrical zone: the Ø before the value

operations.precondition: a drawing with a view, and the datums to be cited already placed

operations.name: note
operations.summary: Writes a text note on the sheet of the drawing, and READS BACK what is written.
operations.details:
Puts a text note on the sheet of a drawing — the general notes: «break all sharp edges», «galvanise after welding», «general tolerances ISO 2768-mK».

I TELL YOU IF IT WAS BORN, not that I called the API: the notes are counted before and after. And I count them for you in TWO separate places — on the sheet and inside the views — because they are two different things and adding them would make an empty drawing look full.

THE TEXT COMES BACK READ by SOLIDWORKS, not copied from what you asked: a note that appears with a different text reads as a right note until someone compares it.

WHERE IT GOES: SHEET coordinates, in millimetres, by default at the top left. If you ask for a point outside the sheet I refuse — outside the sheet the note really exists and is counted, but when printing it does not appear, and no error would say so.

WHAT I CANNOT KNOW is whether what you write is TRUE. I guarantee that the note is there and says what you wrote.

text.description: the text of the note. Required: an empty note takes up a place on the sheet and says nothing.

x_mm.description: distance from the left edge of the sheet, in millimetres. Default 20.

y_mm.description: height from the bottom edge of the sheet, in millimetres. Default 20 mm below the top edge.

operations.precondition: an open drawing, with an active sheet

operations.name: section_view
operations.summary: Creates a section view on a drawing, and checks that the cut met material.
operations.details:
Cuts a view of the drawing and puts the section beside it. It is the first thing that is missing for a real shop drawing: a part with an internal cavity, without a section, cannot be read — the hidden lines say there is a void, not what shape it has.

I DRAW THE CUTTING LINE MYSELF, from side to side of the view: a line that only grazes it gives an empty section without saying anything. By default I cut in the middle; with «offset_mm» you move the cut, in **sheet** millimetres — not of the model, because on the sheet the view is scaled.

I TELL YOU IF IT WAS BORN by counting the views before and after, not because the API answered with an object: it can answer without having done anything. The view I then read (hatch, letter) is the one the call returned; the last view of the sheet only when it returned none, and view_read_from says which. When the section is not born, or the cutting line cannot be selected, the line I drew is removed from the sheet, said removed only after the sheet sketch is counted again.

I REFUSE IF THERE IS NO HATCHING. A section without hatching is a cutting line that fell outside the material: on the sheet there remains a view that looks good and shows nothing, and no error would say so. I prefer to fail and tell you where I cut.

THE LETTER IS ONE PER DRAWING: if «label» already belongs to another section or to a detail I refuse and tell you the ones used — two «A-A» look like the same cut. The letter the view really has I read back to you («label_reread»).

WHAT I CANNOT KNOW is whether that is the section that was needed. I can tell you that the cut met material, not that it passes through the cavity you wanted to show.

view.description: which view to section, by name. Without it, the first model view of the sheet.

orientation.description: how the cutting line runs. Default «vertical».

offset_mm.description: how far to move the cut from the centre of the view, in SHEET millimetres. Positive to the right (or upward). Default 0, that is, in the middle.

label.description: the letter of the section: «A» gives the title «Section View A-A» (in the language of the installation). Default «A».

depth_mm.description: depth of the cut for a partial section. Default 0, which cuts all the way through.

operations.precondition: an open drawing with at least one model view

operations.name: detail_view
operations.summary: Creates an enlarged detail view on a drawing, and checks that the circle became a detail.
operations.details:
Enlarges a piece of a view. It is the other half of what a shop drawing lacks: the section shows what is inside, the detail shows what is too small to read at the scale of the drawing — a groove, a chamfer, a fillet with its dimension.

I DRAW THE CIRCLE MYSELF, inside the view. By default at the centre with a radius of a quarter of the shorter side; with «x_mm» and «y_mm» you move it and with «radius_mm» you change it, in **sheet** millimetres — not of the model, because on the sheet the view is scaled.

I REFUSE IF THE CIRCLE GOES BEYOND THE VIEW: a circle outside enlarges empty space, and the enlarged empty space is still a view that looks good.

AND I TELL YOU IF THE CIRCLE BECAME A DETAIL, counting the detail circles on the source view before and after. If it does not go up I refuse, and remove both the new view and the circle, each said removed only after a reread: left there, they would be a hand-drawn circle next to a view tied to nothing, and no error would say so. The view I read is the one the call returned (view_read_from); when the detail is not born, the circle I drew is removed.

THE LETTER IS ONE PER DRAWING: if «label» already belongs to a section or to another detail I refuse and tell you the ones used. The real letter I read back to you («label_reread»).

WHAT I CANNOT KNOW is whether that is the detail that was needed: a circle moved by ten millimetres enlarges a piece of smooth plane, and is just as valid.

view.description: which view to detail, by name. Without it, the first model view of the sheet.

x_mm.description: how far to move the centre of the circle from the centre of the view, in SHEET millimetres. Positive to the right. Default 0.

y_mm.description: how far to move it vertically, in SHEET millimetres. Positive upward. Default 0.

radius_mm.description: the radius of the circle, in sheet millimetres. Default: a quarter of the shorter side of the view.

scale.description: how many times to enlarge. Default 2, that is, 2:1.

label.description: the letter of the detail. Default «B», because «A» is usually taken by the section.

operations.precondition: an open drawing with at least one model view

operations.name: title_block
operations.summary: Says which properties the title block ASKS FOR and which it SHOWS. Touches nothing.
operations.details:
Reads the TITLE BLOCK of the active sheet and tells you two different things: **which custom properties it asks for** and **which ones it is showing**.

WHY THEY ARE TWO THINGS. A title block does not contain text: it contains links, written `$PRP:"Descrizione"`. Filling it means writing those properties with «set_property».

**THE NAME MUST BE COPIED TO THE LETTER.** If you write it with a capital letter or a space different from the ones the title block references, **nothing visible happens**: SOLIDWORKS writes the property, the title block does not show it, and the PDF comes out with an empty box. No error, anywhere. That is why I give you the exact names instead of leaving you to guess them.

If a property is asked for and not shown I tell you: either it is not written yet, or it is written with another spelling.

Beware of `$PRPSHEET`: it takes the property from the PART in view, not from the drawing. They are two different drawers, and mixing them up means writing on the wrong document.

If the title block has no linked note I tell you, instead of letting you fill in properties that would not appear: that text is drawn inside the sheet format, not fed.

operations.name: interference_check
operations.summary: Says whether the components of the assembly interpenetrate, and by how much volume. Touches nothing.
operations.details:
Looks for the INTERFERENCES between the components of the open assembly: the places where two parts occupy the same space.

WHY IT MATTERS. Two interpenetrating parts open, rebuild, export and print: **there is no error anywhere**, and in the workshop they do not fit. It is the defect you find out about when the part is made.

I TELL YOU THE VOLUME, not only how many there are. Two interferences can be two tenths of a cubic millimeter — two faces grazing each other — or thousands, that is half a lid inside the base. **The count alone does not tell a problem from a detail.**

FACES THAT TOUCH, by default, do NOT count as an interference: otherwise every well assembled assembly would come out broken, because a lid resting on the base shares a face with it. But a shaft in a hole of the same diameter shares the cylindrical surface, and there is exactly the problem: that part does not go in. If that is what interests you, ask me with «touching_counts», and I always tell you which of the two I used.

THE COUNT AND THE LIST MUST AGREE. «how_many» is the count SOLIDWORKS gives; «interferences_read» is how many interferences its list actually held. When the two differ, «volume_total_mm3» is left out (a sum over part of the list would be smaller than the truth) and «what_is_not_known» says what was missing; a count of zero with interferences in the list is refused instead of answered «none».

POSSIBLE interferences (IsPossibleInterference) are counted apart: certain_interferences and possible_interferences, and the verdict counts only the certain ones in its alarm (both null when a flag could not be read). The count of components looked at excludes suppressed components (suppressed_components). The two settings echoed in the answer (touching faces, and interferences inside multibody parts) are the values SOLIDWORKS reads back; if one reads back different from the request, the check is refused.

WHICH PAIR AND WHERE. Each item of «interferences» names its components («components») and its box in the space of the assembly («box_from_mm», «box_to_mm»). With «touching_counts», faces that touch come as CONTACTS: «contact» true, volume 0, counted in «how_many» and in «contacts», never in «volume_total_mm3» nor in the alarm.

It changes nothing: it can also be asked for through «measure».

touching_counts.description: true: two faces that touch exactly count as an interference. It is for «does this shaft go into this hole?». False (default): a lid resting on the base is not an error.

inside_parts.description: true: also looks between the bodies INSIDE the same multibody component. False (default): only between different components.

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least two components

operations.name: drawing_cut_list
operations.summary: Puts the cut list of the weldment on the drawing, and compares it with the one of the part.
operations.details:
Inserts into the drawing the CUT LIST of the weldment behind a view: the list of bars with lengths and quantities.

AND I COMPARE IT. The part already knows, by itself, how many bodies it has in the list; the table on the drawing says its own. They are **two independent readings of the same fact**: if they do not match I tell you and I do not choose which one to believe. A drawing that declares a quantity different from the model sends the wrong number of bars to the shop, and neither side gives an error.

It usually means that the part changed after the last «cut_list»: redo that one and put the table back.

I do not guess the quantity column by position: I ask the table template for it, first by type and then by property name. If I do not find it the comparison is not made, and the answer says so in «comparison_done» (false) instead of in a sentence at the bottom.

THE COLUMNS AND THE PLACE: I keep the ones the shop needs to cut (number, quantity, length, the two angles, description) and hide the others — the house table template has 17, and the table ran off the sheet. «columns» chooses others by header, or «all». Then I measure the table and put it in a free spot inside the frame, outside the views and the title block; if there is no room I remove it and say so.

WHAT THE COMPARISON COUNTS: the bodies of the cut-list folders at the top of the part's tree, in the part's active configuration. The folders of a sub-weldment are not descended into, and the view's configuration is not activated for the count (finding M32, open): on a part with sub-weldments, or with the view on another configuration, a mismatch can be the count's and not the table's.

view.description: which view. Empty = the first of the drawing.

x_mm.description: where to put the top-left corner of the table. Empty = a free spot that I find myself.

columns.description: the headers of the columns to keep, or ["all"]. Empty = number, quantity, length, angles, description.

configuration.description: which configuration of the part: the guide asks for the name of the «As Welded» configuration. Passed as given. Empty: passed empty and SOLIDWORKS picks it; which one has not been measured, and it is not necessarily the view's (finding M32, open).

template.description: the table template. Empty = the one of the installation.

operations.precondition: a drawing with a view of a weldment that already has the cut list

operations.name: new_sheet
operations.summary: Adds a sheet to the drawing, with the same projection angle as the first.
operations.details:
Adds a SHEET to the open drawing and activates it.

I DO NOT ASK YOU FOR THE PROJECTION ANGLE, and it is not a simplification: I read it from the current sheet and pass it on unchanged. If sheet 2 were born in a different angle from sheet 1, the same drawing would have two sheets mirrored differently -- **neither of them gives an error**, and whoever cuts the part from sheet 2 cuts it flipped.

And I read it back from the new sheet after creating it: passing it is not having it. If it does not match I stop.

Size and scale too, if you do not say, are those of the current sheet: two sheets at different scales can be wanted, but not through distraction.

The name, if you do not say, is the next free one in the series SOLIDWORKS started («Sheet2», «Sheet3»... with the word of the installation). A name already used I refuse: two sheets with the same name and you no longer know which one you are looking at.

name.description: what to call it. Empty = the next free name in the series of the sheets («Sheet2»...).

paper_size.description: A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A4V. Empty = the one of the current sheet.

scale_numerator.description: the first number of the scale. Empty = the one of the current sheet.

scale_denominator.description: the second number of the scale. 1:2 is written as 1 and 2.

operations.name: activate_sheet
operations.summary: Brings a sheet of the drawing to the front, by name.
operations.details:
Activates a SHEET of the drawing: from then on the views and the annotations go on that one.

IT IS ASKED FOR BY NAME, not by number. An index would be the perfect occasion to work on the wrong sheet without any error.

I do not believe the answer: after activating it I ask the drawing which sheet it has in front, and if it is not the one you asked for I stop -- otherwise the following steps would work elsewhere.

The names of the sheets are in «inspect_part», under «sheets».

I REFUSE IF THE SHEET DOES NOT EXIST, and I list the ones that do with their names. On a multi-sheet drawing getting the sheet wrong gives no error: the views end up on the active one, and the shop receives a sheet with someone else's stuff on it.

name.description: the exact name of the sheet, as the state reports it. The name is the one SOLIDWORKS gives, in the language of its installation: the example is from an English one; copy the name from the state as it is.

operations.precondition: an open drawing with more than one sheet

operations.name: save_document
operations.summary: Saves the open document.
operations.details:
Saves the active document to disk — part, assembly or drawing.

It also serves as the FIRST STEP of a drawing: a view attaches to the path of the part, so a part never saved cannot be put on a drawing.

The file written is read back: path and size are in the measurements.

The answer carries save_warnings (the swFileSaveWarning_e names, or «none») and save_warnings_note when the model needed a rebuild, had rebuild errors, or had views needing an update. A failed save gives the error and warning names next to the raw codes.

path.description: where to save. If you do not say, it is saved where it already was; a never-saved document without a path is an error.

operations.name: model_view
operations.summary: A named view: isometric, front, top...
operations.details:
Adds to the sheet a NAMED VIEW of the part, at the point you say.

The most useful is the ISOMETRIC one: on its own it makes whoever looks at the drawing understand the part, and the three standard views on their own often do not.

x_mm and y_mm are the position ON THE SHEET, with the origin at the bottom left: on an A3 (420x297) the top right corner is around 320, 220.

view.description: which view; isometric if you say nothing

x_mm.description: position on the sheet from the left, in mm

y_mm.description: position on the sheet from the bottom, in mm

model.description: the path of the part. If you do not say, the first open part is used.

operations.precondition: an open drawing and the part open beside it

operations.name: standard_views
operations.summary: The three standard views, in first-angle projection.
operations.details:
Puts on the sheet the THREE STANDARD VIEWS of the part, in FIRST-angle projection — the one used in Europe.

Third-angle projection does not exist in this catalogue, on purpose: it is a twin call that never fails and produces a drawing with right and left swapped. No measurement notices, and the part is cut mirrored.

The views are counted before and after: if none is born the operation fails, instead of leaving you an empty drawing that looks successful.

CENTRE MARKS ON HOLES. After the views are made the drawing is rebuilt, and the answer gives centre_marks_after_rebuild: the marks SOLIDWORKS put (null when a view cannot be counted). A view made by this call that shows holes end-on and has no centre mark at all gets them from the bridge, through the same walk as the centre-mark check: one mark per hole, each counted on the sheet. centre_marks_added_by_bridge says how many; a view where SOLIDWORKS put some marks, and a view that was on the sheet before, are left as they are. When that happens the answer also gives holes_in_views_without_centre_marks and auto_centre_marks_option (the document option that inserts them, null when it cannot be read). A hole the bridge could not mark is counted in holes_left_without_centre_mark, with centre_marks_note saying what to do.

model.description: the path of the part to put in view. If you do not say, the first open part is used. You find it in «documents_open» in the state.

operations.precondition: an open drawing and the part open beside it

operations.name: check_body_geometry
operations.summary: Says whether the bodies are closed, sound solids. Does not touch the part.
operations.details:
Looks at the BODIES of the part and says whether they are closed solids with no defects.

It does not draw and does not modify anything: it is a question, not an operation. Call it before handing over a part that is going to be printed or exported.

For each body it answers: the type (solid, sheet, wire), how many faces it has, whether it is closed, how many gaps and how many topological defects, with the NAME of the defect and not the number. Then a verdict in one sentence: «printable» means ONE SINGLE solid body, closed, with no defects.

An OPEN body -- a surface left there by mistake -- is the case that matters and the one nobody sees: it gives no error anywhere, it looks like a part, and the STL that comes out of it encloses nothing.

WITH «body_uid» THE VERDICT IS ABOUT THAT BODY ONLY: «printable» and «verdict» speak for it, and «verdict_about» says so («body C2»; «part» when you ask for the whole part). «bodies_in_part» always counts every body of the part: a sound body of a part of two is still a part whose STL is two separate shells.

A body whose defect check (Check3) or gap count (Diagnose) cannot be read is not called sound: its defect list is null with defects_not_read, and the printable verdict is false with the reason.

WARNING about what it does NOT look at: the wall thickness and the overhangs. A shell three tenths of a millimeter thick passes through here without a word.

body_uid.description: a single body, by identifier (for example «C2»). If you do not say it, it looks at all of them. The identifiers are in the document state, inside «bodies». With it the verdict speaks for that body only; «bodies_in_part» still says how many bodies the part has. The identifier is resolved through the document state and checked against its signature (centre and box): if the part changed since and it now names another body, the step is refused. Only the solid bodies of the state have an identifier; to check sheet bodies too, leave body_uid out.

operations.name: check_overhangs
operations.summary: Says what does not print without supports, and by how much. Does not touch the part.
operations.details:
A wall that hangs in the void beyond a certain angle prints as lost filaments. SOLIDWORKS says nothing -- the part is sound, the volume is right, the geometry is closed -- and the defect shows only on the machine, once the print is finished.

I LOOK AT EVERY SURFACE, the curved ones too: the underside of a horizontal cylinder hangs in the void in its lower part and not in its upper part, so one normal per face is not enough. I tessellate and look triangle by triangle, weighting by area.

THE ANGLE IS COUNTED FROM THE VERTICAL, as in slicers: a straight wall is 0, a horizontal ceiling is 90, and «threshold 45» means that beyond 45 the support is needed. It is not the angle with the plane, which is the complement: two numbers that look alike and say the opposite.

WHAT RESTS ON THE PLANE I DO NOT COUNT. The bottom face looks straight down -- 90 degrees, the worst case -- but it rests on the plane of the machine and prints perfectly well.

I answer with the worst overhang, how much area hangs, and the faces one by one with where they are, so you know whether to turn the part or chamfer.

I ALSO LOOK AT HIDDEN BODIES (how many there are I tell you in «hidden_bodies»). A curved face that cannot be tessellated I cannot look at: I count it in «faces_not_analyzed», and if I found no overhangs elsewhere «prints_without_supports» is null, not true.

threshold_deg.description: beyond how many degrees from the vertical the support is needed. Default 45, which is the normal value for a filament printer; 30-35 to be on the safe side, 60 if the machine cools well.

print_direction.description: the direction the print grows in, three numbers. Default [0, 0, 1]. Changing it is the way to ask «what if I printed it turned?» without turning the part.

body_uid.description: a single body (for example «C2»). If you do not say it I look at all of them.

operations.name: file_dependencies
operations.summary: Which files the document depends on, and which are missing on the disk. Touches nothing.
operations.details:
An assembly (or a drawing) is a graph of files on the disk: I tell you which files it depends on, at every level, and for each one whether it is there. A file that is missing is a component that the assembly shows SUPPRESSED: before measuring or exporting it must be found again or replaced.

If it is missing, the disk says so, not the API: the parameter that promises to mark broken references does not mark them (measured).

The paths are where each file was last saved (GetDependencies with Searchflag false): with the search rules, a component that is not loaded could come back as another file with the same name found in another folder, which exists, and a missing file would not be reported (measured, L12-8).

operations.name: mass_properties
operations.summary: Volume, area, mass and center of gravity of the part. Touches nothing.
operations.details:
Answers «how much does this part weigh»: volume, surface area, mass, density and center of gravity.

MASS WITHOUT A MATERIAL IS NOT ZERO, IT IS «UNKNOWN»: if the part has not been given a material I answer null and I tell you why. SOLIDWORKS would answer all the same, using the default density of the model -- usually 1000 kg/m3, that is water -- and a steel part that weighs like water is a believable number and wrong by a factor of eight. Use «apply_material» first.

The mass also arrives RECALCULATED by hand (volume times density) next to the one from SOLIDWORKS: if the two diverge, one of the measures is not in the units it declares, and it is the way a factor of a thousand shows itself instead of hiding.

ON AN ASSEMBLY I weigh the whole assembly (suppressed components not, and I list them) and I check the mass against the sum of the parts read one by one: if they do not match I stop. If a part has no material, the mass is null and I tell you which.

WHICH COMPONENTS WEIGH ON AN ASSEMBLY (measured). Suppressed components do not weigh, and they are listed. ENVELOPES do not weigh: SOLIDWORKS leaves them out of the assembly mass, the sum of the parts leaves them out too, and the answer names them in «envelope_components». HIDDEN components weigh, as SOLIDWORKS weighs them, and are named in «hidden_components_weighed». LIGHTWEIGHT parts refuse the step: SOLIDWORKS would weigh them, but their material cannot be read while they are lightweight, so a part without material would weigh as water unseen, and the sum of the parts cannot read them. Resolve them in SOLIDWORKS, or pass «resolve_lightweight»: true and I resolve them first; they stay resolved, and «lightweight_resolved_on_request» says so. If one is still lightweight after that, I refuse. A component whose load state cannot be read refuses the step too, and so does one that is neither a part nor a sub-assembly by its file extension or its document.

WITH «body_uid», a body named from an earlier reading of the state is checked against its signature (centre and box): if the part changed since and the identifier now names another body, the step is refused instead of weighing the other one.

body_uid.description: a single body, by identifier (for example «C2»). If you do not say it, it weighs them all together. A body named from an earlier reading of the state is checked against its signature (centre and box): if the part changed since and the identifier now names another body, the step is refused instead of weighing the other one.

resolve_lightweight.description: assembly only: when some parts are lightweight, resolve them first (ResolveAllLightWeightComponents) instead of refusing. Default false. They stay resolved, and the answer says so in «lightweight_resolved_on_request».

operations.name: body_bounding_box
operations.summary: The box of the part in mm, body by body and all together.
operations.details:
Answers «does it fit in the 300x260x40 box»: from where to where the part reaches on each of the three axes, and how big it is.

The points are the TRUE ones of the body, taken in six directions, not the approximated box: a bounding box declared larger than the real one makes everything around it be sized wrong.

It is the box ALIGNED TO THE AXES of the model, not the smallest possible one: a long part placed diagonally has a much larger bounding box than the one it would need turned the right way, and this measure does not say how to turn it.

ON AN ASSEMBLY I measure each part in the place where it sits in the assembly and the box that contains them all; suppressed components not, and I list them.

ON AN ASSEMBLY, LIGHTWEIGHT PARTS ARE MEASURED without resolving them: GetBodies3 reads the bodies of a lightweight part (measured), and the answer names them in «lightweight_components_measured». Envelopes and hidden components are in the box too, named in «envelope_components» and «hidden_components». A component whose load state cannot be read refuses the step, and so does one that is neither a part nor a sub-assembly by its file extension or its document.

body_uid.description: a single body, by identifier (for example «C2»). If you do not say it, it measures all the bodies and the box that contains them. A body named from an earlier reading of the state is checked against its signature (centre and box) before it is measured: if the part changed since and the identifier now names another body, the step is refused instead of measuring the other one. The answer names the body by the identifier asked.

operations.name: cosmetic_thread
operations.summary: Says «there is a thread here» on a pin or a hole that already exists. It cuts nothing.
operations.details:
Puts a COSMETIC THREAD on the round edge of a pin or a hole: it is an annotation, not a cut. The volume of the part stays what it was, and if it changes I fail -- it would mean the thread was really cut.

Use it when the thread is on a pin or on a hole made by hand: for a threaded hole made with the wizard there is already «hole_wizard», which takes the dimensions from the standard.

IT ATTACHES TO THE EDGE, not to the face: the circular edge of the cylinder or of the hole.

WATCH THE DESIGNATION: the text you write -- «M6x1» -- is what ends up on the drawing, WORD FOR WORD. This SOLIDWORKS call ignores the standard and the size: there is no table that checks whether «M6x1» is right for a Ø6 pin. If you write it wrong, it reaches the shop wrong.

edge_uid.description: the ROUND edge to attach the thread to, taken from the document state (for example «E3»).

designation.description: the text of the thread, for example «M6x1». It ends up on the drawing as written here.

depth_mm.description: how deep the thread is, in mm. Not needed if it is through.

through_all.description: true: the thread goes all the way through, and the depth is not needed.

diameter_mm.description: the diameter, if you want it checked: if it does not match the edge's, I tell you instead of threading the wrong edge. If you do not give it, I measure it from the edge.

operations.name: variable_fillet
operations.summary: A fillet that changes radius from one end of the edge to the other.
operations.details:
Rounds an edge with a radius that VARIES: large on one side, small on the other.

It is for where the part has to take a load at one point and has no room at the other -- a bracket that widens toward its mounting, the edge of a cover that thins out. For a fillet that is the same from end to end there is «fillet_edges».

The edge must be open, with two ends: on a circle -- the edge of a hole -- there is no «from» and «to» to vary between.

The larger radius must fit on the edge: if it exceeds half of its length I say so before trying. And afterwards I check that it really removed material: a feature that is made without removing anything leaves the edge sharp, and the tree grown for nothing.

edge_uid.description: the edge to fillet, taken from the document state (for example «E7»).

start_radius_mm.description: the radius at one end of the edge, in mm.

end_radius_mm.description: the radius at the other end, in mm.

operations.name: fillet_face
operations.summary: A fillet resting on two faces instead of an edge: the radius ball rolls touching both.
operations.details:
Rounds the transition between TWO FACES: the surface that results is the one left by a ball of the requested radius rolling in contact with both. On the edge between two faces that touch it gives the same part as «fillet_edges»; the difference is that you do not need to name an edge, the two faces are enough.

On an OUTSIDE edge it removes material, in an inside corner it adds some: the answer says how much the volume changed and in which direction.

THE HAND CALCULATION IS A CHECK, NOT A SIDE NOTE. When the two faces are flat, at 90 degrees and touch along an edge, the expected change is edge length x r^2 x (1 - pi/4), read before the fillet («expected_change_abs_mm3»). A volume change further from it than 0.05 mm3 (or one ten-thousandth of it, whichever is larger) is refused: the fillet is removed, the part is checked back, and the answer says so. On any other pair of faces the expected change is null and nothing is compared.

I REFUSE IF the same face is in both sets (for the edges of a single face there is «fillet_edges»), and IF the two faces are flat and PARALLEL; both are checked before any attempt. Of two parallel faces, if they face the same way, or turn their backs on each other like the front and the back of a block, no ball touches both. Two walls that face each other (a slot) I let you try only with a radius equal to half the distance, and I tell you.

AFTERWARDS I CHECK: that the new feature is a fillet, that the volume has changed, that the bodies are the ones from before and that no feature has gone into error. If one of these does not hold I remove the fillet, check again that the part is as it was, and tell you. If it is not created -- usually the radius, which does not fit on the faces -- I say so and point you to «fillet_edges».

One face per set; faces are named with the identifiers of the state, not with a reference to a step.

face_1_uid.description: the first face, taken from the document state (for example «F1»).

face_2_uid.description: the second face, different from the first (for example «F3»). Two flat parallel faces are not filleted together.

radius_mm.description: the radius of the fillet, in mm. It must fit on both faces.

operations.name: combine_bodies
operations.summary: Unites, subtracts or intersects two or more bodies of the same part.
operations.details:
The boolean between BODIES of the same part: «union» fuses them into one, «subtract» removes the others from the main one, «intersect» keeps only what they have in common.

It serves molds and jigs, and parts designed as several bodies and then put together. Separate bodies are made with «move_bodies» and its copy option.

IN A SUBTRACTION THE ORDER CHANGES THE PART: the main body is the one that REMAINS, the others are the ones cut out of it. If you do not say which, it is the first, and I write it in the answer.

Which bodies: the identifiers of the state (C1, C2...) with «_uid», or the bodies of an earlier step of this same plan with «_ref». After a cut the identifiers read before are no longer valid, and I refuse an old uid instead of combining another body.

After the union I count the bodies: if there are still two, they did not fuse -- usually they do not really touch -- and I fail instead of confirming a part different from the one you think you have.

After a boolean the identifiers of bodies and faces are NO LONGER valid: read the part again.

IF YOU DO NOT SAY WHICH BOOLEAN I do «union», and it is written in the answer. «subtract» and «intersect» are asked for by name, because they change the part in opposite ways.

operation.description: which boolean to do. If you do not say, it is «union», and I write it in the answer.

main_body_uid.description: the body that REMAINS (for example «C1»). If you do not say, it is the first. It matters only for «subtract», but writing it never hurts.

main_body_ref.description:
the body that REMAINS, if an earlier step of this same plan creates it (for example after a cut, which changes the identifiers). Give this OR main_body_uid, not both. The step must leave ONE body only.

Allowed kinds:
- bodies: the bodies touched by that step

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

tool_bodies_uid.description: the bodies to unite, subtract or intersect with the main one. If you do not say, all the others.

tool_bodies_ref.description:
the bodies to unite, subtract or intersect, if an earlier step of this same plan creates them. Give this OR tool_bodies_uid, not both.

Allowed kinds:
- bodies: the bodies touched by that step, all together

step.description: the number of the step that creates the geometry, counting from 1. It must be an EARLIER step than this one.

operations.name: minimum_distance
operations.summary: How far apart two faces or two edges are, checking that the number is not contradicted by its own points.
operations.details:
Measures the SHORTEST distance between two faces, two edges, or a face and an edge. It is the way to answer «how much material is left between the gasket groove and the outer face»: two named things and a number, instead of a hand calculation on the bounding box.

It also answers with the TWO POINTS between which it measured, and with their distance calculated separately: if the number and the points do not match, the call failed and answered all the same, and in that case I fail instead of giving you the number.

Zero means that the two things touch, and I tell you.

start_uid.description: identifier of the first face or of the first edge, taken from the document state (for example «F3» or «E7»).

operations.name: measure_between
operations.summary: The measuring tool: area, perimeter, distance, angle, parallelism between one or two entities.
operations.details:
Measures ONE face or edge -- area, perimeter, length, radius -- or TWO, and then it also says distance, differences on the three axes, angle, whether they are parallel or perpendicular.

It is the same measuring tool that is used by hand in SOLIDWORKS. For the minimum distance alone between two things, «minimum_distance» is more robust: it checks the result against the points.

What does not apply does not come back: the perimeter of a face that has none, the radius of a plane. SOLIDWORKS would give them as -1, which is a number and is not one.

A distance to an arc or a circle is taken as «arc_measure» says: centre to centre (the default), between the nearest points or between the farthest points. The result says which one was used («arc_measure», read back from SOLIDWORKS) and «projection»: none. Measured on two holes D10 and D20 at 50 mm centres: centre 50, minimum 35 (the wall between them), maximum 65. I refuse any other value of «arc_measure».

uid.description: the face or edge to measure, taken from the document state.

uid2.description: the second one, if you want to measure BETWEEN two things.

arc_measure.description: how a distance to an arc or a circle is taken: centre = centre to centre (the default), minimum = between the nearest points, maximum = between the farthest points. The distance between the centres is always given too, centre to centre.

operations.name: export_stl
operations.summary: Writes the STL for 3D printing, in millimetres. It checks the part first, and refuses if it is not a closed solid.
operations.details:
Writes the part as STL, the format that the slicers of 3D printers read.

BEFORE WRITING I call «check_body_geometry» and I REFUSE IF the part is not a single closed solid body without defects. It is not caution: an STL carries nothing that says the part was right -- it opens, slices and prints all the same, and the hole shows when the part is in your hand. If you know what you are doing, «export_anyway»: true writes it all the same and tells you so in the answer.

THE UNITS ARE ALWAYS MILLIMETRES, forced by hand before writing and put back as they were after. The file does not carry them and the slicer assumes millimetres: exported in inches, the part comes out 25.4 times smaller and no error says so.

After writing I READ THE FILE BACK: how many triangles it says it has and whether its size matches that number. An STL that does not match is a file that opens and is not the part.

The answer carries save_warnings (the swFileSaveWarning_e names, or «none») and save_warnings_note when the model needed a rebuild or had rebuild errors; preferences_not_restored names any user preference that could not be put back. A failed save gives the error and warning names next to the raw codes.

path.description: where to write the file, .stl extension included. If you do not say, the path of the part with the extension changed is used, and then the part must already have been saved.

quality.description: «fine» (default) makes more triangles and follows the curves better; «coarse» makes a smaller file and facets the round parts.

binary.description: true (default): binary file, much smaller. False: ASCII, readable but ten times bigger.

export_anyway.description: writes the file even if the check says no. Default: false. Use it only knowing what was wrong.

operations.name: export_step
operations.summary: Writes the STEP for whoever has to machine the part, and reads back from the file which protocol actually came out.
operations.details:
Writes the part as STEP: it is the format in which a part is sent to a supplier, to a customer, or taken to another CAD.

Unlike the STL it does NOT REFUSE if the part has several bodies or surfaces: a STEP carries them, and a weldment is sent to the supplier exactly like that. The check runs all the same and its verdict comes back in the answer, so you know what the part you sent was like.

AFTER WRITING I READ THE FILE BACK and say which protocol REALLY came out, not which you asked for: the value that governs it is a number with no name in the API, and the only proof is the FILE_SCHEMA written inside the file. If it does not match, it fails -- some suppliers accept only AP203.

With «reopen_and_compare» the file is reopened in SOLIDWORKS and its volume compared with the part: it is the only measurement that says the GEOMETRY survived the translation. It costs a document opening, so it is not the default.

ALSO AN ASSEMBLY: I write it whole and count the solids in the file against those of the unsuppressed parts. I refuse «reopen_and_compare» on an assembly: reading back the STEP of an assembly opens a window and the call does not return. An instance changed in the assembly (a cut: user bodies in GetBodies3's BodiesInfo) is a shape of its own and counts all its bodies; the other instances count once per file and configuration. WHICH COMPONENTS THE FILE HOLDS (measured): HIDDEN components are not written by SOLIDWORKS, so they are left out of the expected count and named in «hidden_components_not_exported». LIGHTWEIGHT components are resolved by SOLIDWORKS to write the file and stay resolved; the count is made after the export, and «lightweight_resolved_by_the_export» says how many were resolved. Envelopes are written and counted.

AP242 IS WRITTEN BY SOLIDWORKS MBD, not by a protocol number: in SOLIDWORKS 2021 the protocol preference takes only 203 and 214, and 242 written there gives an AP203 file (measured). I write AP242 through PublishSTEP242File, with the part brought to the front. Without the MBD licence (the bench machine has none) I refuse, saying so; AP214 and AP203 are still available. With AP242 the path must end in .stp. When the file is written, its FILE_SCHEMA is read back as for the other two.

The answer carries save_warnings (the swFileSaveWarning_e names, or «none»; null for AP242, whose call has no warnings mask) and save_warnings_note when the model needed a rebuild or had rebuild errors; preferences_not_restored names any user preference that could not be put back. A failed save gives the error and warning names next to the raw codes.

path.description: where to write the file, extension included: .step or .stp for AP214 and AP203, only .stp for AP242 (a .step path is refused before writing). If you leave it out, the part's own path is used with the extension changed.

protocol.description: AP214 (the default) also carries the colours; AP203 is the oldest and the most widely read. AP242 is not a protocol number: it is written only by SOLIDWORKS MBD (PublishSTEP242File), needs the SOLIDWORKS MBD licence and a path ending in .stp. Without the licence I refuse and say so, and a file already at the path stays as it was.

reopen_and_compare.description: reopens the file just written and compares the volume with the part, failing beyond a thousandth of difference. Default: false, because it costs a document opening. The reopened file is closed by reference, never by its title (with the default path its title is the part's own stem); if it cannot be closed safely it stays open and the answer says so. The document that was in front is brought back by its path.

operations.name: export_iges
operations.summary: Writes the IGES, for the CADs and machines that do not read STEP.
operations.details:
Writes the part as IGES. It is for when on the other side there is a CAD or a machine that does not read STEP: it is an older and less precise format, and between the two STEP is always the first choice.

Like the STEP, it does not refuse for several bodies or surfaces, and the check of the part comes back in the answer.

After writing I count the parameter records of the file: an IGES with only the headers and nothing inside exists, weighs something and opens.

Three IGES options of the SOLIDWORKS profile would add curves to the file or turn the solid into curves: «IGES wireframe (3D curves)», «Export 3D Curve features» and «Export sketch entities». I turn them off for the export and put them back as they were. After writing I also read the file's directory and count its solids (type 186) and surfaces: «solid_entities», «surface_entities», «entities». A file with neither, curves only, is refused: it opens, and it is not the part. After turning the three options off I read them again: «iges_options_not_off» lists any that stayed on or could not be read (empty is the proof they were off), and «iges_options_warning» says what to do.

The answer carries save_warnings (the swFileSaveWarning_e names, or «none») and save_warnings_note when the model needed a rebuild or had rebuild errors; preferences_not_restored names any user preference that could not be put back. A failed save gives the error and warning names next to the raw codes.

path.description: where to write the file, .iges or .igs extension included. If you do not say, the path of the part with the extension changed is used.

representation.description: «solids» (default) writes the bodies as BREP, and it is what whoever has to machine the part needs; «surfaces» writes trimmed faces.

reopen_and_compare.description: reopens the file just written and compares the volume with the part. Default: false. The reopened file is closed by reference, never by its title (with the default path its title is the part's own stem); if it cannot be closed safely it stays open and the answer says so. The document that was in front is brought back by its path.

operations.name: weldment_profiles
operations.summary: Lists the profiles of the library and their sizes, written as they must be copied. Touches nothing.
operations.details:
Says which profiles there are -- tubes, IPE, angles, flat bars -- and for each one which sizes, written exactly as they must be copied.

CALL ME BEFORE «structural_member» and «rectangular_frame». They want «profile_path» and «configuration» TO THE LETTER, and to the letter really means it: upper case, spaces and commas count. A size written almost right GIVES NO ERROR -- SOLIDWORKS uses the active configuration of the profile, the part comes out with a different wall from the one you think, the rebuild is clean, and you find out in the workshop.

I read the files without opening them: I open no documents and leave nothing lying around.

If the library is large I give you the first forty and tell you so: with «search» and a piece of the name you narrow them down.

search.description: a piece of the profile name, to narrow down: for example «IPE», «HEA», or a word of the file name such as «tube», in the language the library files are named in. Without it, it lists them all.

with_measurements.description: true (default) to get the sizes of each profile as well. False if all you need is to know which profiles exist: it costs less.

operations.name: mate
operations.summary: Constrains two components to each other, taking one face from each. It is the difference between an assembly and a tidy heap.
operations.details:
Puts a mate between two components of the open assembly.

FACES ARE NAMED BY DIRECTION, not by identifier: «the lower face of C2 on the upper face of C1». The components are the ones «inspect_part» lists as C1, C2, ... and those identifiers are STABLE (unlike the identifiers of the faces of a part, which are renumbered at every reading).

THE DIRECTIONS ARE THE ASSEMBLY'S: the faces come from the component's bodies in the part's own coordinates, and each normal is turned with the component's placement in the assembly (Transform2) before it is compared, so on a turned or mirrored component «up» is the face that looks up in the assembly. If no flat face looks that way I say so instead of taking one at random; if the placement of the component cannot be read, I refuse without touching anything.

Among several faces that look the same way I take THE LARGEST: on a cover or a plate that is the one you want.

WHEN THE LARGEST IS NOT THE ONE, OR THE FACE IS CURVED, name it by a point on it: {"point_mm": [x, y, z]} in mm of the assembly (the state gives «origin_mm» and «axes» of each component, so a point of the part file can be carried into the assembly). I take the face of that component within 0.05 mm of the point; a point no face reaches, or one on an edge between two faces, is refused with the distance read.

WHAT THE MATE BLOCKS IS MEASURED (Z-C14). SOLIDWORKS gives no remaining degrees of freedom from here, so before the mate and after it each non-fixed component of the pair is moved 5 mm along X, Y and Z and turned 5 degrees about X, Y and Z of the assembly, one move at a time with a rebuild after each: a direction the mates put back is blocked, one where the component stays is free. The answer gives, per component in the order of the two ids, blocked_directions_before and blocked_directions_after (TX, TY, TZ, RX, RY, RZ), degrees_removed and direction_test; a fixed component is not moved (fully blocked by definition), and neither is one inside a sub-assembly (unknown). After the test each component is set back where it started, and so is any other component the rebuilds carried along; a slide the rebuild leaves is reported in residual_drift_mm and in the answer, not hidden.

A REDUNDANT MATE IS REFUSED: when the mate blocks nothing that was not already blocked, on a pair where one component is fixed or already fully blocked, I take out the mate I have just made (the object AddMate5 returned, never a name) and refuse, saying which directions were already blocked. SOLIDWORKS itself reports nothing wrong on such a mate (AddMate5 answers NoError, GetWhatsWrongCount stays 0): this test is the only place it shows. When a position cannot be set or read, a move comes back only in part (neither blocked nor free), the assembly does not rebuild cleanly (a feature or mate in error makes every rebuild answer false), or neither component is fixed or fully blocked, I say so and keep the mate: a mate is never called redundant from a reading that could not be made.

THE COST: 13 rebuilds per non-fixed component for each reading (two per direction and one to put it back), and two readings per mate: 26 for the usual pair of a fixed and a free component, 52 when both move. On a large assembly this takes a while.

I do not rely on the answer of the call: I count the mates of the two components before and after, and if they did not increase I tell you instead of declaring it done.

WHERE THE COMPONENTS ENDED UP is in the answer: «placement_after» gives «origin_mm» and «axes» of both, read after the mate, and the verdict says them. A distance mate also gives «face_b_along_normal_a_mm», the signed distance of face B from face A along the normal of face A, measured on the faces: choose the side with «distance_side».

If one of the two faces cannot be selected, the step is refused and AddMate5 is not called.

component_a.description: the identifier of the first component, from «inspect_part»: «C1», «C2», ...

face_a.description: which of its faces: by direction, one of up, down, right, left, front, back (directions of the assembly: on a turned component, the face that looks that way after the rotation), or by a point on it, {"point_mm": [x, y, z]} in mm of the assembly, for any face, flat or curved.

component_b.description: the identifier of the second component.

face_b.description: which of its faces: a direction or {"point_mm": [x, y, z]}, as «face_a».

variant.description: coincident (default), parallel, perpendicular, distance, concentric or tangent. Concentric and tangent want a curved face, so at least one of the two faces must be named by a point: between two faces named by direction (always flat) I refuse them.

distance_mm.description: only for «distance»: how far apart they are. Without it I refuse -- there is no reasonable default value.

distance_side.description: only for «distance»: on which side of face A face B ends. along_normal_a (the default) is the side face A looks at: «down» of C1 at 11.7 mm puts C2 11.7 mm BELOW C1. against_normal_a is the other side. The side is measured after the mate and a mate on the wrong side is taken out.

alignment.description: «aligned» (the default) or «opposite»; any other value I refuse. If SOLIDWORKS refuses for alignment, try the other: two faces that look at each other want «opposite».

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least two components

operations.name: mirror_component
operations.summary: Mirrors a component on a plane of the assembly: the right and the left bracket.
operations.details:
Mirrors a component on a plane of the assembly (front, top, right). YOU MUST CHOOSE HOW, because they are three different parts:
- «instance»: the same file, mirrored. Correct for a symmetrical part.
- «opposite_linked»: a new file that FOLLOWS the original. Change the right one and the left one changes too.
- «opposite_unlinked»: an INDEPENDENT new file. Correct the right one and the left one stays as it was, and nothing tells you.

Afterwards I verify it: the centre of the new part against the mirror of the centre of the original, and for the opposites the feature tree of the new file (linked or not). The new file takes the name of the original with the «suffix» (default «_spec»), in the same folder.

I REFUSE IF you do not give me «mode» (I explain the three), if the plane is not one of the three of the assembly or if the component is not there (I tell you which ones there are).

The three planes are recognised by their geometry (the plane's normal through the origin), not by their place in the tree nor by their name: if no plane of the assembly has that normal through the origin, I refuse and say what I read.

For an instance of the same file the orientation of the new instance is SET («orientation», default mirrored_x_mirrored_y) and then CHECKED on the axes of the instance (Transform2): the centre is the same in all four orientations and cannot tell them apart. The answer carries «orientation» and «new_axes» (x, y, z unit vectors). «orientation» with an opposite-hand mode is refused, and so is a value that is not one of the four.

A mirror born with a rebuild error (GetErrorCode2) is refused and removed. Whenever a refusal removes the mirror it made, it says so only after reading the tree again and not finding it there; otherwise it asks you to remove it.

component.description: the identifier of the component, from the state: «C1», «C2», ...

orientation.description: only for an instance of the same file: how the new instance is turned, as SOLIDWORKS names it (swMirrorComponentOrientation2_e). Default mirrored_x_mirrored_y, the SOLIDWORKS default. Refused with an opposite-hand mode.

plane.description: the plane of the assembly to mirror on.

mode.description: instance (same file), opposite_linked (new file that follows the original), opposite_unlinked (new independent file).

suffix.description: for the opposites: what to add to the file name. Default «_spec».

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least one component

operations.name: fix_component
operations.summary: Fixes or frees a component of the assembly, and reads it back.
operations.details:
Fixes a component (it no longer moves, whatever mates it has) or frees it (only its mates hold it). It is the only state of a component that changes how the assembly rebuilds.

FIXED DOES NOT MEAN MATED: SOLIDWORKS fixes the first component inserted by itself, and an assembly that stays still only because of that is not assembled. After changing it I read it back, and I tell you how many mates it has: a free component with zero mates is resting, it moves.

I REFUSE IF you do not give me «grounded» (true or false: they are two opposite things, there is no default) or if the component is not there (I tell you which ones there are).

TOP-LEVEL COMPONENTS ONLY: a component inside a sub-assembly («top_level»: false in the state) is refused, and the refusal names the sub-assembly that holds it and its uid; IsFixed and FixComponent work on the top level only. Open the sub-assembly to fix one of its parts, or fix the sub-assembly itself.

component.description: the identifier of the component, from the state: «C1», «C2», ...

grounded.description: true to fix it, false to free it.

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least one component

operations.name: suppress_mate
operations.summary: Turns a mate of the assembly off, or back on, by its uid or name, and reads it back.
operations.details:
Turns a mate off without losing it: the components it held stay where they are, but the directions it blocked are free. «reactivate»: true turns it back on. It is the road back from a wrong mate, and it can be walked back, so it asks no confirmation.
