THE MATE IS NAMED from «mates_list» in the state of the assembly: its uid («M1» is the first mate of the tree, renumbered when one is deleted) or its name as SOLIDWORKS writes it («Distanza1» in an Italian session, «Distance1» in an English one). I read it back after the change.

I REFUSE IF the mate is not there (I tell you which ones there are) or if it is already as you ask (nothing changes, and I say so).

mate.description: the uid («M1», «M2», ...) or the name of the mate, from «mates_list».

reactivate.description: true to turn a suppressed mate back on. Default false: suppress it.

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least one mate

operations.name: delete_mate
operations.summary: Deletes a mate of the assembly by its uid or name, and reads back that it is gone.
operations.details:
Deletes a mate. It cannot be undone with another operation, only with «undo»: the bridge asks the person for a confirmation before running a plan that contains it, when the client can ask (MCP «elicitation»); when it cannot, the plan runs and the answer says in «confirmation» that nobody was asked. To turn a mate off and keep it, use «suppress_mate».

THE MATE IS NAMED from «mates_list» in the state of the assembly, by uid («M1») or by name, as in «suppress_mate». I read back that the name is gone and that there is one mate fewer.

I REFUSE IF the mate is not there (I tell you which ones there are).

mate.description: the uid («M1», «M2», ...) or the name of the mate, from «mates_list».

operations.precondition: an open assembly with at least one mate

operations.name: place_component
operations.summary: Puts a component where you say and turns it as you say, and reads the placement back.
operations.details:
Sets the placement of one component of the open assembly: «origin_mm» is where its origin goes, in mm of the assembly (the same field the state answers for each component), and «rotation» turns its axes: one turn {axis, angle_deg} or a list of them, applied in order, about the axes X, Y, Z of the ASSEMBLY, starting from the part's own axes (so the same request gives the same placement wherever the component was). Right-hand rule: 90 degrees about z takes x to y. What you do not send stays as it is.

IT IS READ BACK after a rebuild: the answer gives «origin_mm» and «axes» as read («+X -Y -Z» means the component's x points to +X of the assembly, its y to -Y, its z to -Z; three unit vectors when an axis is not on an axis of the assembly), «moved_mm» and «turned_deg» from where it was. The state lists «axes» for every component too.

MATES WIN: a component its mates hold is moved back by the rebuild. Then I refuse, set it back where it was, and say how far the mates took it: place it before mating, or suppress the mate first.

I REFUSE IF the component is fixed (free it with «fix_component» first), if it is inside a sub-assembly (its placement would move the whole sub-assembly), if you send neither «origin_mm» nor «rotation», or if one of them is not in the form above.

component.description: the identifier of the component, from the state: «C1», «C2», ...

origin_mm.description: [x, y, z] in mm of the assembly: where the origin of the component goes. Without it the origin stays where it is.

rotation.description: {"axis": "x" | "y" | "z", "angle_deg": number}, or a list of them applied in order, about the axes of the assembly, starting from the part's own axes. Without it the component keeps its orientation.

operations.precondition: an open assembly with a component that is not fixed

operations.name: replace_component
operations.summary: Changes the file of a component that is already mounted, and tells you whether the constraints survived SOUND or merely survived.
operations.details:
«The cover has to be redone»: changes the file of a component that is already mounted.

ALWAYS LOOK AT WHAT I ANSWER ABOUT THE MATES. Measured: the constraints of the old part **stay** -- they are not lost -- but staying does not mean working. A constraint that pointed at a face of the old part survives in the tree and may go into ERROR, and then the count still sees it and everything looks fine.

**A broken constraint is worse than a missing one**: a missing one shows, a broken one seems to hold. So I tell you two things, not one: how many mates there are before and after, AND how many problems the document has before and after. If the problems increased I shout it, and the thing to do is to remove those constraints and put them back with «mate».

THE NEW FILE MUST ALREADY BE OPEN in SOLIDWORKS, as for «insert_component»: copy the path from «documents_open».

I REFUSE IF you give the component the file it already has: it would succeed and change nothing, and you would believe you had changed the part.

THE CONFIGURATION IS CHECKED, NOT YET CHOSEN. A «configuration» the new file does not have is refused before the swap, and nothing changes. The swap asks SOLIDWORKS to match the configuration of the old component with one of the new file (its «match name» choice); the choice that uses the named configuration waits for a probe that shows it opens no window. So after the swap I read back the configuration the new component references and give it in the answer («configuration»), and, when you asked for one, «configuration_as_asked»: false means SOLIDWORKS took another one, the verdict opens with a WARNING, and the swap stays (undo it if the size matters).

TOP-LEVEL COMPONENTS ONLY: a component inside a sub-assembly is refused before the call (ReplaceComponents2 wants a top-level component). The swap counts as done only when a component took up the new file that was not on it before AND the chosen component no longer uses its old file: another component already mounted on the new file does not count. «took_its_place» names the component(s) that took it; the C1..Cn numbers follow the names, so read the state again before naming one by uid.

component.description: the identifier of the component to replace, from «inspect_part»: «C1», «C2», ...

path.description: full path of the NEW file, already open in SOLIDWORKS.

configuration.description: a configuration of the new file, whole name. Refused before the swap if the file does not have it. SOLIDWORKS matches the old component's configuration by name, so the one you get may differ: the answer reads it back («configuration_as_asked»). Empty: not checked; the guide says an empty name means the default configuration of the new file.

all_instances.description: true (default): if the same part is mounted several times, it replaces all of them. False: only that one.

operations.precondition: an open assembly, and the new file already open

operations.name: insert_component
operations.summary: Puts an already open part into the open assembly, and tells you whether it is constrained or merely resting there.
operations.details:
Inserts a component into an assembly.

WHAT YOU MUST KNOW BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: inserting is NOT mating. The part appears, the tree fills up, the rebuild is clean -- and the component is resting there, free. Four free components look like an assembly, they open, they turn, they export, and they are put together wrong.

So I answer with «grounded», «mates» and «resting». Not fixed and zero mates means RESTING: the part is just sitting there, and as long as it is so the assembly is not assembled, it is a tidy heap.

WHAT I CANNOT TELL YOU, and I say so: **how much** a component is still free. SOLIDWORKS does not give me the residual degrees of freedom from here -- it answers «not available» on every component, fixed or free -- and an invented number would be worse than no number. So «resting: false» means «it has at least one mate», NOT «it no longer moves». One coincident mate leaves three of the six directions free (measured), and «mate» says which directions each mate blocks.

THE COMPONENT MUST ALREADY BE OPEN in SOLIDWORKS: I look for it by path, and on a closed file the insertion answers «not done» without saying why. The paths you can use are the ones in «documents_open» of the state: copy them from there.

«configuration» chooses the configuration of the part to mount. The name is checked against the configurations of the open file BEFORE inserting, compared whole (the part in angle brackets included): a name the file does not have is refused and nothing is inserted. Then SOLIDWORKS is asked for it (UseConfigForPartReferences true) and the configuration the new component really references is read back: if it is another one, the component is taken out again and the step is refused, and the refusal says whether the removal was confirmed by counting the components. Without a name the component comes in with the file's last saved configuration (swAddComponentConfigOptions_CurrentSelectedConfig), and the answer's «configuration» says which one.

WATCH THE COORDINATES, because the two numbers do not match and it is not an error: «x_mm, y_mm, z_mm» place the **centre of the bounding box**; «origin_mm», which I answer and which you will read back in the state, is where the part's **origin** ended up. If the part has its origin on a face -- that is, almost always -- the two points are half the extent apart. Ask for z=30 on a part 4 thick and the origin comes out at z=30 but y=-2: neither number is wrong, they are two different things.

I do not rely on the answer of the insertion: I count the components before and after, and if they did not increase by one I tell you instead of declaring it done.

path.description: full path of the file to insert, copied from «documents_open». It must already be open in SOLIDWORKS.

x_mm.description: where the CENTRE of the component's bounding box goes, in mm. Default 0. It is not a mate: it is only where to rest it. And it is NOT where its origin ends up: if the part has its origin on a face, the origin moves by half the extent. I answer with «origin_mm» for this.

y_mm.description: where the CENTRE of the bounding box goes, in mm. Default 0.

z_mm.description: where the CENTRE of the bounding box goes, in mm. Default 0.

configuration.description: the configuration of the part to mount, by its whole name (the part in angle brackets included). A name the file does not have is refused before inserting; the component comes in with it, read back, or is taken out again. Empty: the file's last saved configuration.

origin_mm.description: [x, y, z] in mm of the assembly: where the part's ORIGIN goes, instead of x_mm, y_mm, z_mm (sending both is refused). Applied after the insertion and read back, as «place_component» does.

rotation.description: {"axis": "x" | "y" | "z", "angle_deg": number}, or a list of them in order, about the axes of the assembly: how the part comes in turned. Read back with the origin; a placement that does not come back as asked takes the component out again.

operations.precondition: an open assembly, and the component to insert already open

operations.name: circular_sweep
operations.summary: A solid tube of given diameter along a path of points. On a straight path I check that the volume is area times length.
operations.details:
Makes a shape that follows a path: a cable gland, a handle, a bent tube. It is the first operation of the catalogue that makes something that is not straight.

THE PROFILE IS A NUMBER, not a sketch: you give the diameter and that is all. The path is a list of points in space, and I draw it myself: I do not ask you for a sketch because in the document state sketches have no identifier, and you would have no way to point one out to me.

ON A STRAIGHT PATH THE CALCULATION IS DONE BY HAND, and I do it: the volume must be the area of the circle times the length, and if it is not I refuse. On a path with elbows it is not -- at the elbows the material overlaps and the real volume is smaller -- and then I give you the theoretical one, telling you it is an upper limit, not the answer.

A BEND TIGHTER THAN THE RADIUS OF THE TUBE cannot be made: the surface would cross itself. In that case SOLIDWORKS creates nothing and does not say why; I tell you.

path_mm.description: the points of the path, at least two, each [x, y, z] in mm. For example [[0,0,0], [100,0,0]] makes a straight tube 100 long.

diameter_mm.description: the diameter of the tube, in mm.

operations.name: loft_two_circles
operations.summary: A transition between two circles of different diameter, and I tell you by how much it departs from the truncated cone.
operations.details:
Blends two different round sections: a reducer, an inlet, a transition from a large tube to a thin one.

A LOFT BETWEEN TWO CIRCLES IS NOT A CONE, and it is the thing worth knowing. Its surface is a spline approximation of the cone: the volume departs from the formula of the truncated cone by a few thousandths of a percent, always on the low side. I give you both numbers and the difference, so you do not chase a defect that is not there. If you need the exact cone, «revolve» on a trapezoid does it.

The two circles lie on planes parallel to the one you choose, at the distance you say. You can offset them from each other to make an oblique transition.

plane.description: the plane of the first circle. Default «front».

diameter1_mm.description: the diameter of the first circle, on the chosen plane.

distance_mm.description: how far the second circle is from the first, in mm. Greater than zero: the second circle goes on the side the chosen plane faces (+Z for front, +Y for top, +X for right). A negative or zero distance is refused.

offset1_mm.description: how far to move the first circle sideways. Default 0.

offset2_mm.description: how far to move the second one sideways: needed for an oblique transition. Default 0.

operations.name: sketch_picture
operations.summary: Puts a photo or a hand sketch, to scale, on a plane: to trace over.
operations.details:
Puts an image (a photo of the part, a sketch with dimensions in pen) into a sketch on a plane, TO SCALE: you tell me how wide the whole image really is («width_mm» — a known measure divided by its pixels, times the image's width in pixels) and where its lower left corner goes. Then you trace over it on the same plane with the sketch operations.

I VERIFY THE SCALE: the first and the last pixel of the first row, in the sketch, must be as far apart as the millimetres per pixel say, within 1%. I answer with the rule for going from a pixel to millimetres.

I REFUSE IF it is a PDF (it cannot be inserted: convert it to PNG), a file that does not exist or is not an image, or a width that is not positive.

Over 2048 px SOLIDWORKS compresses the picture in a part, even with HighestResolution (measured: 4096 x 2048 is held as 2048 x 1024). «pixel» and «mm_per_pixel» are the FILE's, the pixels you count in the image: the scale is «width_mm» divided by the FILE's pixel width. «solidworks_pixels» is the map SOLIDWORKS holds, and «compression» says when the two differ. I also refuse when the file's pixel size cannot be read and SOLIDWORKS holds 2048 px or more on a side, and when the picture SOLIDWORKS holds does not have the file's shape. I also refuse when SetSize or SetOrigin answers false, or when the width, height or lower left corner read back is more than 0.01 mm from what was asked; the picture then stays in the sketch, to be removed.

path.description: the image file: PNG, JPG, BMP, GIF or TIF.

plane.description: the plane to put it on.

width_mm.description: how wide the WHOLE image really is, in mm: the scale.

x_mm.description: where the lower left corner goes, x. Default 0.

y_mm.description: where the lower left corner goes, y. Default 0.

operations.precondition: an open part (even an empty one)

operations.name: plane_three_points
operations.summary: An oblique plane, given by three points; I read its normal back to tell you it is the one asked for.
operations.details:
«create_plane» can only make a plane OFFSET from one of the three standard ones: it serves everything that is aligned with the axes and nothing else. For a tilted hole, an oblique face or a bracket at 30 degrees there was no plane to draw on.

THE POINTS ARE COORDINATES, not vertices of the part: three triples of numbers in millimetres, in the model's coordinate system. I do not ask you to point me at vertices because in the document state vertices have no identifier -- faces and edges do, vertices do not.

I CHECK THAT THE PLANE IS THE RIGHT ONE. From the three points I compute the normal, then I read back that of the plane just created and compare the two: if they do not coincide I refuse. «One more feature in the tree» would say the same of a crooked plane, and on a crooked plane you would draw without noticing.

THREE POINTS IN A LINE DO NOT MAKE A PLANE, and I tell you before trying: infinitely many planes pass through a line.

point1_mm.description: the first point, three numbers in mm: [x, y, z].

point3_mm.description: the third point. It must not lie on the line through the other two.

operations.name: base_flange
operations.summary: A sheet metal part bent from an open profile: thickness, bend radius, depth.
operations.details:
Makes a SHEET METAL part from an open profile drawn on a base plane: an L, a U, a Z. Every corner of the profile becomes a bend with the radius asked for.

THE POINTS ARE THE INNER FACES when the profile goes in the direction in which the thickness stays on the RIGHT: measured on an L of 50 + 30 given from the top towards the right, the flat pattern comes out 80.712 mm, equal to the hand calculation on the inner faces. Given the other way round, the thickness goes to the other side and the points become the OUTER faces: the answer always says which of the two («points_are_faces»), because between the two there are 2 times the thickness per bend.

The answer also carries the FLAT PATTERN: the length of the flattened part measured by SOLIDWORKS, next to the one calculated by hand with the K factor read back from the part. If they do not match, it says so, before the DXF goes to cutting.

I REFUSE IF a segment is shorter than the bends that eat it (a 1 mm side with a radius of 2): SOLIDWORKS would give a red feature without saying which side. I also refuse a flange that is born in error or that adds less than half of the material of the hand calculation.

If the flat pattern does not unsuppress (or suppress again) when I measure the flat length, the answer says so in flat_pattern_problem (the part may be left flattened).

plane.description: the base plane the profile lies on. Default «front».

points.description: the OPEN profile, at least two points [x, y] in mm on the plane. An L: [[0,30],[0,0],[50,0]].

radius_mm.description: the INNER radius of the bends

depth_mm.description: how deep the sheet is, perpendicular to the plane

operations.precondition: a part with no bodies, or one to add a sheet metal body to

operations.name: edge_flange
operations.summary: A new bend on a border edge of a sheet metal part that already exists.
operations.details:
Adds a 90 degree FLANGE on a border edge of a sheet metal part (made with «base_flange»): this is how a box is closed, with bends on edges of different directions.

The edge is the one between the wide face of the sheet and an END face, as wide as the thickness; the flange rises on the side the wide face faces. «length_mm» is measured to the OUTER VIRTUAL SHARP, and the material stays inside the bounding box as before: the side you bend on gets shorter by radius + thickness. Thickness, radius and K factor are those of the sheet, read back.

The answer carries the added volume next to the hand calculation (the extra flat pattern, (L - R - T) + BA - (R + T), times the thickness and the length of the edge), and the length read back from the flange.

I REFUSE IF the length leaves nothing straight (not beyond radius + thickness), if the edge is not straight or is not on the border of the sheet, or if the flange is created without adding material.

If the flat pattern does not unsuppress (or suppress again) when I measure the flat length, the answer says so in flat_pattern_problem (the part may be left flattened).

edge_uid.description: the border edge to bend, from the document state (E1, E2...)

length_mm.description: how long the flange is, measured to the outer virtual sharp

operations.name: hem
operations.summary: The edge of a sheet metal part folded back on itself, closed or open.
operations.details:
Folds the edge of a sheet metal part (made with «base_flange») back on itself: the hem that removes the sharp edge and stiffens the border. «closed» is flattened against the sheet; «open» leaves «gap_mm» between the edge and the sheet. It stays inside the bounding box as before.

The edge is the one between the wide face and an end face, as wide as the thickness. The answer carries the added volume next to the hand calculation: for the open one it is the 180 degree bend with the inner radius equal to half the gap, measured three times to the thousandth; for the closed one the calculation uses a radius of 0.05 mm, measured with thickness 2, and it is stated but does not decide.

I REFUSE IF the hem does not leave anything straight, if «open» has no gap, if the edge is not straight or is not on the border, or if the hem is created without adding material.

If the flat pattern does not unsuppress (or suppress again) when I measure the flat length, the answer says so in flat_pattern_problem (the part may be left flattened).

edge_uid.description: the border edge to fold, from the document state (E1, E2...)

variant.description: closed (flattened) or open (with a gap). Default «closed».

length_mm.description: how long the folded edge is

gap_mm.description: only for «open»: the space between the folded edge and the sheet

operations.name: sketched_bend
operations.summary: Bends a sheet metal part along a line drawn on one of its faces.
operations.details:
Bends a sheet metal part that already exists along a LINE drawn on one of its planar faces, from the point «start_mm» to the point «end_mm» (points [x, y, z] in mm on the plane of the face). The line crosses the face from edge to edge.

The sheet bends towards the side the face FACES: to bend the other way, draw the line on the other face. The radius is that of the sheet; which side stays fixed is chosen by SOLIDWORKS, and the answer carries the bounding box before and after.

A bend does not add sheet: volume and flat pattern stay what they were, and if they change the answer says so.

I REFUSE IF the angle is not between 0 and 180 degrees exclusive, if the face is not planar, if an end of the line is not on the face, or if the bend is created without bending anything.

If the flat pattern does not unsuppress (or suppress again) when I measure the flat length, the answer says so in flat_pattern_problem (the part may be left flattened), and before bending I refuse if that happens.

face_uid.description: the planar face the line is drawn on, from the document state (F1, F2...)

start_mm.description: one end of the bend line, [x, y, z] in mm on the face

end_mm.description: the other end, [x, y, z] in mm on the face

operations.name: flat_pattern_dxf
operations.summary: The DXF of the flat pattern of a sheet metal part, for cutting.
operations.details:
Writes the FLATTENED sheet metal part to a DXF: the drawing that goes to the cutting machine.

THE PART MUST BE SAVED: on a part with no file SOLIDWORKS opens «Save As» and waits for someone to click — measured. I refuse such a part before calling SOLIDWORKS.

The DXF is READ BACK: its bounding box must have the flat pattern measured on the part as its long side, otherwise I refuse it — a DXF of something else opens just the same. Without «path» it goes next to the part, with its name.

If the flat pattern does not unsuppress (or suppress again) when I measure the flat length, the answer says so in flat_pattern_problem (the part may be left flattened).

path.description: where to write the .dxf. Default: next to the part, with its name.

operations.name: dimension_scheme
operations.summary: Dimensions the part in the model with DimXpert, from three reference faces.
operations.details:
Puts on the PART (not on a drawing) the dimensions that a draftsman would put: thicknesses, sides, hole diameters and their position from the datums. It is the DimXpert of SOLIDWORKS, from the core, with no add-ins.

THE DATUMS ARE THREE PLANAR FACES, in order: the primary (usually the resting one), the secondary and the tertiary (two perpendicular sides). The position dimensions start from them. With fewer than three it refuses: DimXpert would not refuse, it would put a single dimension.

The answer carries the VALUES of the dimensions («values_mm»), read from the dimensions created: it is the way to see whether it dimensioned what was needed. The answer of SOLIDWORKS to the call («auto_dimension_scheme_response») is False even when it did dimension — measured: it is not looked at.

references_uid.description: THREE planar faces from the document state: primary, secondary, tertiary

tolerance.description: plus/minus on the dimensions (default) or geometric tolerances

operations.name: draft
operations.summary: Tilts faces by an angle, relative to a face that stays fixed. Measures the angle on the part, not on the feature.
operations.details:
The draft angle: the walls of a part made in a mold must lean by a degree or two, or the part does not come out of the form. It also serves castings and features with a draft angle.

TWO DIFFERENT FACES, AND THEY MUST NOT BE CONFUSED. The NEUTRAL face is the one that stays fixed: it is the plane the angle is measured from, and it goes in «neutral_face_uid». The faces to tilt go in «faces_uid». If you swap them, SOLIDWORKS makes a feature all the same, gives it the same name and reports no error -- but it has drafted other faces, by another amount. I notice and I stop you.

HOW I NOTICE. The feature, when the angle is requested, always declares what you asked it for -- even when it has not tilted anything. So I count the faces of the part that really are at the right angle to the neutral one, before and after, and if not enough have appeared I refuse.

THE DIRECTION. With «flip» the wall leans the other way: the part grows instead of shrinking. I answer how much material moved and in which direction, so you see it without looking at the part from the side.

FLAT FACES ONLY: a drafted cylindrical face becomes conical and does not have a single inclination, so I do not count it.

neutral_face_uid.description: the face that STAYS FIXED, the angle is measured from it (for example «F1»). Usually it is the bottom or the mouth of the mold.

faces_uid.description: the faces to tilt. They must touch the neutral one.

angle_deg.description: by how much to tilt them, in degrees. For a mold 1-3 degrees; for a sand casting even 5.

flip.description: true to make the walls lean the other way -- the part grows instead of shrinking. Default false.

operations.name: rib
operations.summary: A stiffening rib: fills, in the plane of a line, the space between the line and the walls of the part. Measures the material added.
operations.details:
Stiffens a thin wall: the corner of an L bracket, the bottom of a hollowed box. You give a LINE with two ends «start_mm» and «end_mm» (points [x, y, z] in mm in the model system) that lies on a plane: one of the three base planes («plane»), possibly moved parallel to itself by «distance_mm» (I create the offset plane myself). The rib grows IN the plane of the line, from the line to the walls that the line -- extended -- meets, and it is «thickness_mm» thick, split in half between the two sides of the plane.

THE LINE LIES IN THE EMPTY SPACE, with its ends (or their extension) on the walls to be joined. Example: L 60x60, 10 thick and 50 deep, front plane at distance 25, line from [10, 40, 25] to [40, 10, 25]: the rib is the triangle in the corner, 450 mm2 x 6 = 2700 mm3.

THE DIRECTION OF THE MATERIAL I try myself: first as given, then flipped, and I keep the first one in which the rib is created and the part grows. It depends on the shape (in the L it is the one as given, in the hollowed box the flipped one) and the answer says which I used and how many attempts. If the line lies between walls on both sides, the one as given wins.

I REFUSE IF an end of the line is not on the plane given (I do not project it silently), IF the line is shorter than one millimeter, and IF the rib is created in neither of the two directions: usually it means there is nothing to meet from the line, as on a plate without walls (for a raised feature on a flat face there is «extrude_on_face»). When I refuse I remove the sketch and the plane I had made: the part stays as it was.

I do not make drafted ribs and I do not look at WHICH walls the rib has joined: I measure that it was created, the material added and that the part did not break.

plane.description: the base plane parallel to that of the rib: front (XY), top (XZ) or right (YZ)

distance_mm.description: by how much the plane of the rib is moved from the base plane, along its normal (+Z, +Y, +X). Negative for the other direction. Default 0: the rib lies on the base plane.

start_mm.description: one end of the line, [x, y, z] in mm, on the plane of the rib

end_mm.description: the other end, [x, y, z] in mm, on the plane of the rib

thickness_mm.description: the thickness of the rib, in mm, split in half between the two sides of the plane. For a bracket 10 thick, usually 4-6.

operations.name: suppress_instance
operations.summary: Removes one or more copies from a pattern already made, and refuses if the copy was not there.
operations.details:
A grid of holes that skips one where a rib passes, a row of slots that stops before the bend. The pattern is made first, whole, with «linear_pattern» or «circular_pattern»; then what must not be there is removed.

COPIES ARE COUNTED FROM 1, AND THE ORIGINAL IS NOT A COPY. In a row of four, 1 is the first after the original and 3 is the last.

I REFUSE IF THE COPY WAS NOT THERE, and that is the reason this operation checks instead of just writing. A pattern builds only the copies that fit in the material and answers «succeeded» even when it made fewer than were asked for: asking to remove the fourth of four, when the fourth fell outside the part, SUCCEEDS and changes nothing. I count the faces before and after, and if they did not drop I tell you that copy was not there and put everything back as it was.

A removed copy can be put back with «reactivate».

NOT ALL PATTERNS CAN DO IT: those driven by a sketch, a chain or a dimension do not have numbered copies. A mirror has a single copy: it is removed by deleting it. A FILL pattern and a TABLE-driven pattern do skip instances, but a fill pattern skips them by (row, column) and a table pattern by the rows of its table: I do not translate a copy number into those, and I refuse them by name.

FROM A TWO-DIRECTION GRID I DO NOT REMOVE COPIES (linear, circular or curve-driven): SOLIDWORKS numbers them row by row, and a single number does not say which position. I also refuse if after the change the pattern goes into error, is left without faces, or loses faces that are not worth the removed copies — and I put it back as it was. For this reason I also refuse copies FUSED with each other or with the part in a way that changes the number of faces (for example two slots that touch): the face count does not add up and I cannot say what I removed. In the answer «faces_per_copy» says how many faces a copy is worth (null if I could not read it: then this check was not done).

feature_uid.description: the PATTERN to remove copies from (for example «L3»), not the repeated feature. The identifiers are in the document state, inside «feature».

copies.description: the numbers of the copies to remove, counting from 1 after the original. For example [2] removes the second copy.

reactivate.description: true to PUT BACK copies removed earlier, instead of removing more. Default false.

operations.name: engrave_text
operations.summary: Engraves (or embosses) a text on a flat face, and refuses if the text does not fit.
operations.details:
Writes WORDS into the part: serial number, mounting direction, customer name, «UP». Engraved (default) or embossed.

I CHECK THAT IT FITS FIRST, AND IT IS HALF OF THE JOB. The width of a text cannot be calculated from the string: it depends on the font, and «PROVA» 10 mm high in Century Gothic is 47 mm wide. A text that runs off the face is cut away SILENTLY -- the feature comes out green, and in the part there is «PRO». I read where the letters really end and I refuse, telling you by how much it overflowed.

I ANSWER HOW WIDE AND HIGH IT REALLY IS, so the second time you already know which numbers to pass.

The anchor is the start of the text at the bottom left: from there it goes to the right. The area of the letters that I answer goes with the square of the height -- doubling «height_mm» quadruples the area -- and it is the way to check two markings against each other.

NOT ON A CURVED FACE: wrapped text is another feature, which I do not have.

face_uid.description: the flat face to write on (for example «F1»). The identifiers are in the document state.

x_mm.description: where the text starts on the face, in mm, in the coordinates of the face. Default 0.

y_mm.description: the other coordinate of the anchor. Default 0. The anchor is the BOTTOM LEFT CORNER of the text, not its center.

height_mm.description: the height of the letters in mm. Default 5.

depth_mm.description: how deep to engrave, or how high to raise if «raised». Default 0.5 mm, which is a marking you can read. For one you can feel by touch you need 0.3-0.8 mm.

raised.description: true for an embossed text instead of an engraved one. Default false. Embossed prints better in 3D, engraved reads better on a machined part.

font.description: the name of the font, for example «Arial». If you do not say, I use the document's. A font that is not on this computer changes the width of the text.

bold.description: true for bold: thicker letters, which read better on a 3D print or a casting. Default false.

operations.name: set_property
operations.summary: Writes a custom property -- drawing number, revision, customer -- on the document or on a configuration.
operations.details:
Writes a custom property: it is what ends up in the title block of the drawing and in the PDM data card. «Numero disegno» (drawing number), «Revision», «Cliente» (customer), «Descrizione» (description).

THE DOCUMENT AND A CONFIGURATION ARE TWO SEPARATE DRAWERS. A property written on the document is NOT SEEN from a configuration, and the other way round: they are not inherited. If you say «configuration» I write it there and only there; if you do not say it I write it on the document and only on the document. I repeat it to you in the answer every time, because it is the error that gives no error: the drawing number is written on the document, read back from the configuration, it is not there, and nobody says why. «scope» says it outright: «file», «configuration» (the one you name, or the active one) or «both», which writes it in the two and reads it back from each.

IF IT ALREADY EXISTS, I REPLACE IT. I do not let you believe you changed a revision that stayed the one it was.

AFTER WRITING I READ BACK. The command answers a code, not the value: if on reading back I do not find what I wrote I fail instead of confirming a data card that is not the one you think.

A value written as a formula (for example "SW-Mass@part.SLDPRT") is checked as the TEXT written, and resolved_value gives what SOLIDWORKS evaluates it to, when the two differ.

name.description: the name of the property, for example «Numero disegno» or «Revision». Write it as you want to see it in the title block: the name is what whoever reads the data card will see.

value_text.description: the value to write. Empty string to clear it.

configuration.description: the name of the configuration to write it on. If you do not say it I write it on the DOCUMENT, and that is a different place. The names are in the document state, inside «configurations».

scope.description: where: «file» is the document, «configuration» the one named in «configuration» or else the active one, «both» the document and that configuration. Left out: «configuration» if you name one, «file» otherwise. «file» together with a configuration named is refused.

operations.name: create_configuration
operations.summary: Makes a variant of the part -- left and right, with and without a hole -- and activates it at once.
operations.details:
Creates a configuration: the same bracket left and right, with and without a hole, in a single file. It is how a shop that works to drawings asks for a family of parts.

IT CREATES IT AND ACTIVATES IT. SOLIDWORKS moves the document onto the new configuration at once, without being asked: everything you draw afterwards, and everything the state tells you afterwards, is about THAT one. I tell you in the answer. To go back to another one there is «activate_configuration».

THE NAME I ANSWER WITH IS THE ONE TO USE, and it is not certain to be the one you asked me for: SOLIDWORKS names can have angle brackets inside, and those are part of the name. Report it as it is.

I REFUSE IF A CONFIGURATION WITH THAT NAME ALREADY EXISTS. Two configurations with the same name are not a harmless duplicate: the features suppressed in one and active in the other make two different parts with the same name, and the bill of materials counts one.

name.description: the name of the configuration, for example «Left» or «No hole». If there is already one like that I refuse.

details.description: the description that will appear in the list of configurations.

operations.name: activate_configuration
operations.summary: Switches to a configuration that already exists, and verifies that it really switched.
operations.details:
Moves the document onto another configuration. From here on what you draw and what the state tells you are about that one.

THE NAME IS NOT WHAT IT SEEMS. The default configuration is often called «Default<As Machined>» and NOT «Default»: what is in angle brackets is part of the name. Asked for «Default», SOLIDWORKS answers no, silently -- and often there is more than one configuration that starts with «Default» (a weldment has the pair «<As Machined>» and «<As Welded>»), so there is not even a right way to guess. I DO NOT GUESS: copy the whole name from «configurations» in the document state. The names come in the language of the installation.

AFTER ASKING I CHECK WHICH ONE IS ACTIVE NOW: it is not enough for me that the command said yes, because working for half an hour on the wrong variant gives no error.

I REFUSE IF THE CONFIGURATION DOES NOT EXIST, and I list the ones that do. And the name must be WHOLE: Default is not enough if it is called Default<As Machined>. A partial name I do not guess, because guessing would mean activating the wrong configuration silently.

name.description: the WHOLE name of the configuration to activate, copied from «configurations» in the document state. Suffix in angle brackets included, if there is one.
